recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Chicken and Mushroom Pasta
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of creamy chicken and mushroom pasta rests in a round, off-white ceramic bowl on a well-used wooden dining table. The golden-brown, 2 cm seared chicken cubes are nestled amongst the al dente pasta strands, which are thoroughly coated in a rich, pale cream sauce. Sliced, earthy brown mushrooms are interspersed throughout, adding depth. A scattering of fresh, vibrant green chopped parsley provides a pop of color on top. The dish is presented casually, as if just served from the stove, with the pasta naturally piled. The lighting is warm and natural, suggesting a cozy family kitchen setting. A simple fork rests beside the bowl on a plain cloth napkin, emphasizing the homely, unpretentious comfort of the meal.
instructions: Boil a large pot of salted water. Add pasta. Cook according to package directions until al dente. Drain pasta. Reserve 120ml pasta water.
Pat chicken breast cut into 2 cm cubes dry. Season with salt and pepper.

Heat olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Add chicken cubes. Sear until golden brown and cooked through, about 5-7 minutes. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken from pan. Set aside.

Reduce heat to medium. Add butter to the same pan. Add diced onion. Sauté until softened, about 3-4 minutes. Add sliced mushrooms. Cook until mushrooms are browned and tender, about 5-7 minutes. Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a simmer. Stir in heavy cream and grated Parmesan cheese. Cook, stirring constantly, until sauce thickens slightly, about 3-5 minutes.
Add cooked chicken back to the pan with the sauce. Add drained pasta. Toss to coat everything evenly. If sauce is too thick, add reserved pasta water, a little at a time, until desired consistency.
Taste and adjust seasoning. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley and extra grated Parmesan.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken and Mushroom Tagliatelle
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Pan-Seared Chicken and Mushroom Tagliatelle is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The tagliatelle, glistening with a creamy, light golden sauce, is loosely mounded in the center. Interspersed throughout the pasta are tender, sautéed brown mushroom slices and finely diced onion, adding earthy tones. Four thick, golden-brown pan-seared chicken chunks, cooked to a juicy finish, are artfully placed on and around the pasta, showcasing their crisp exterior. A vibrant sprinkle of fresh, bright green chopped parsley garnishes the dish, providing a pop of color and freshness. The plate is positioned on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by standard silver flatware and a folded cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's textures and inviting warmth, creating an authentic casual bistro ambiance.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with additional grated Parmesan cheese on the side.
Offer crusty bread for dipping in the sauce.
Pair with a light Italian white wine.
instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat 15ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken breasts 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown and internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken. Set aside.
Add remaining 15ml olive oil and butter to the skillet. Add diced onion. Sauté 3-4 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic and sliced mushrooms. Cook 5-7 minutes until mushrooms are tender and browned.
Pour in white wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the skillet. Reduce liquid by half.
Add chicken broth. Bring to a simmer. Stir in heavy cream.
While sauce simmers, cook tagliatelle according to package instructions until al dente. Reserve 120ml pasta water. Drain pasta.
Slice cooked chicken breasts into thick chunks.
Add cooked tagliatelle to the sauce. Add grated Parmesan and chopped parsley. Toss to coat. Add reserved pasta water as needed for desired consistency.
Return chicken chunks to the skillet. Gently combine with pasta. Serve immediately.
notes: Adjust the amount of pasta water to achieve desired sauce consistency.
Ensure chicken reaches a safe internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Mediterranean Chicken Pasta
recipes.special_requests: Mediterranean cuisine, Multicooker, healthy, tasty, spicy, some sauce
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous serving of Spicy Mediterranean Chicken Pasta rests in a simple, deep ceramic bowl on a well-used wooden kitchen table. The al dente penne pasta is coated in a rich, vibrant red tomato sauce, studded with tender, browned chicken chunks (3-4 cm). The sauce shows flecks of diced tomato, minced garlic, and dried oregano and thyme, with visible red chili flakes. A few fresh basil leaves are casually scattered on top for a pop of green. The presentation is homely and inviting, with a natural, slightly asymmetrical arrangement. The lighting is warm and natural, suggesting a cozy family dinner setting. A rustic linen napkin and a fork are placed beside the bowl. The dish fills the bowl comfortably, showcasing its hearty, comforting nature.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread for dipping in the sauce.
instructions: Cut chicken thighs into 3-4 cm chunks.
Set multicooker to Sauté function. Add olive oil.
Brown chicken chunks on all sides. Remove chicken from multicooker. Set aside.
Add diced onion to multicooker. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic, dried oregano, dried thyme, and red chili flakes. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in tomato paste. Cook for 2 minutes.
Pour in diced tomatoes and chicken broth. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom.
Return chicken chunks to the multicooker.
Add penne pasta. Ensure pasta is mostly submerged in liquid.
Secure multicooker lid. Set to Pressure Cook on High for 5 minutes.
Once cooking is complete, perform a Quick Release of pressure.
Open lid carefully. Stir pasta and sauce to combine. Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Serve immediately, garnished with fresh basil leaves.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Cacciatore
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of rustic chicken cacciatore served in a shallow, cream-colored ceramic bowl with minor surface imperfections. Two whole, bone-in chicken thighs are the centerpiece, their skin appearing dark golden and tender from braising. The chicken is partially submerged in a thick, chunky tomato sauce featuring visible pieces of softened translucent onions and whole black olives. A single fresh rosemary sprig is placed casually on top. The bowl sits on a weathered dark wood kitchen table. Beside the bowl is a thick piece of torn crusty bread. The scene is illuminated by warm, soft overhead kitchen lighting, creating a cozy, authentic Italian home-dining atmosphere. A simple linen napkin and a stainless steel fork are placed to the left of the bowl.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty sourdough bread to soak up the tomato sauce
Pair with a side of simple polenta or rustic mashed potatoes
Traditional family-style dining involves placing the skillet in the center of the table
instructions: Season chicken thighs with salt and pepper on all sides.
Heat olive oil in a large deep skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken skin-side down for 6 minutes until golden brown.
Flip chicken and sear for 4 minutes. Remove chicken from skillet.
Add diced onion to the skillet. Sauté for 5 minutes until soft.
Stir in minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add crushed tomatoes, oregano, and the rosemary sprig.
Place chicken back into the skillet, nestled into the sauce.
Simmer on low heat for 30 minutes until chicken reaches 75°C internally.
Stir in the olives 5 minutes before serving.
notes: Use bone-in thighs for maximum flavor and protein content
Ensure the sauce reduces until thick to concentrate the savory tomato profile
Always check the thickest part of the chicken for a safe internal temperature of 75°C

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Baked Chicken and Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Creamy Baked Chicken and Rice is presented in a deep, rustic ceramic bowl on a well-worn wooden dining table. Golden-brown chicken thighs, cooked whole, are nestled atop a bed of creamy, tender white rice. The rice is studded with small diced carrots, celery, and onions, offering subtle flecks of orange and green. The top surface of the casserole, where cheese was added, shows a light golden crust. The dish has a natural, slightly irregular texture, characteristic of a comforting home-cooked meal. A simple, everyday ceramic plate holds the portion, with a metal fork resting casually beside it. A casually folded cloth napkin is nearby. The scene is bathed in warm, inviting kitchen lighting, evoking a relaxed, lived-in family atmosphere with minimal background clutter.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple green salad.
Serve with crusty bread for dipping.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Season chicken thighs with salt, pepper, garlic powder, onion powder, and paprika.
Sear chicken thighs 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown. Do not cook through.
Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside.
In the same skillet, add diced onion, celery, and carrots. Sauté 5-7 minutes until softened.
In a large 3-liter baking dish, combine uncooked rice, chicken broth, cream of mushroom soup, and sautéed vegetables. Stir well.
Nestle the seared chicken thighs into the rice mixture.
Cover the baking dish tightly with foil.
Bake for 35 minutes.
Remove foil. If using, sprinkle shredded cheddar cheese over the chicken and rice.
Bake uncovered for another 15-20 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C and rice is tender and liquid is absorbed.
Remove from oven. Let rest 5 minutes before serving.
Garnish with dried parsley.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
Adjust seasoning to your preference.

recipes.recipe_name: Berenjena Confitada con Piloncillo y Crema de Azahar
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Berenjena Confitada con Piloncillo y Crema de Azahar is elegantly presented on a clean, round white porcelain dessert plate. A small, artfully mounded cluster of glistening, deep amber-brown confited eggplant cubes (approx. 2cm) forms the centerpiece, their surfaces reflecting the syrup's richness. Beside the eggplant, a soft, off-white swirl of delicate orange blossom crema provides a creamy contrast. A single, golden-brown, crisp tortilla shard stands vertically, adding height and a textural counterpoint. Two fresh, vibrant green mint leaves are strategically placed to introduce a pop of color and freshness. The arrangement is balanced and professional, with ample negative space around the elements. The plate rests on a smooth, light wooden table surface, suggesting a modern bistro setting. A simple, neatly folded white cotton napkin is positioned beside the plate. Natural, even lighting from the side creates soft, appealing shadows, highlighting the dish's textures and colors. The background is minimally blurred, maintaining focus on the food while implying a refined but approachable restaurant environment.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve alongside a small glass of chilled Café de Olla.
Offer a small scoop of vanilla bean ice cream as an alternative to the crema.
instructions: Peel eggplant completely. Cut into 2 cm cubes. Place in a colander. Sprinkle with a pinch of salt. Let sit for 30 minutes to drain excess moisture. Rinse well. Pat dry with paper towels.

Break piloncillo into smaller pieces. In a saucepan, combine piloncillo, water, cinnamon stick, star anise, and orange peel. Bring to a simmer over medium heat. Stir until piloncillo dissolves completely. Reduce heat to low.

Add eggplant cubes to the piloncillo syrup. Ensure eggplant is submerged. If not, add a little more water. Simmer gently for 45-60 minutes. Cook until eggplant is very tender and translucent, absorbing the syrup's color and flavor. Remove from heat. Let eggplant cool in the syrup.

For the crema, chill a mixing bowl and whisk attachment. Pour heavy cream into the cold bowl. Add powdered sugar and orange blossom water. Whip on medium-high speed until soft peaks form. Do not over-whip.

Preheat oven to 160°C (325°F). Cut each corn tortilla into two or three triangular or rectangular shards. Place on a baking sheet. Bake for 8-10 minutes. Cook until crisp and lightly golden. Watch carefully to prevent burning.

To serve, gently lift confited eggplant pieces from the syrup. Arrange a small, mounded cluster of eggplant on each of four white dessert plates. Place a dollop or swirl of orange blossom crema beside the eggplant. Insert one crisp tortilla shard vertically into the eggplant or crema for height. Garnish with one or two fresh mint leaves.
notes: This dessert offers a unique sweet application for eggplant, transforming it into a tender, aromatic confection through traditional Mexican candying techniques.
Ensure eggplant is thoroughly drained and patted dry after salting to prevent bitterness and allow better syrup absorption.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Chicken and Vegetable Risotto
recipes.visual_description: The dish presents a single, generous portion of creamy, free-flowing risotto, served in a clean white porcelain bowl. The risotto, a pale, inviting beige, is studded with vibrant green broccoli florets and bright red bell pepper cubes, contrasting beautifully against the creamy rice. Succulent, golden-brown chicken chunks are interspersed throughout the risotto, showcasing their seared exterior. Fresh basil leaves are gently mixed in and scattered over the top, providing a pop of fresh green. The texture is smooth and velvety, indicating the creamy consistency. The bowl sits on a simple light wooden table surface, accompanied by a folded cotton napkin and standard flatware. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's warmth and freshness, with a softly blurred bistro-style background creating a casual yet refined atmosphere. The overall presentation is inviting and approachable, with moderate negative space.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with freshly grated Parmesan cheese.
A side of crusty bread.
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large, deep pan or Dutch oven over medium heat.
Add diced chicken. Cook until browned and cooked through, about 6-8 minutes. Internal temperature should reach 75°C. Remove chicken from pan and set aside.
Add diced onion to the same pan. Sauté until translucent, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic and diced bell pepper. Cook for another 3-4 minutes until softened.
Add Arborio rice to the pan. Stir for 2 minutes until rice grains are coated and slightly translucent at the edges.
Pour in white wine. Stir constantly until liquid is absorbed.
Begin adding warm chicken broth, one ladleful at a time. Stir continuously. Allow each ladleful to be almost fully absorbed before adding the next. This process will take about 20-25 minutes.
After about 10 minutes of adding broth, add broccoli florets to the risotto. Continue adding broth and stirring.
When risotto is creamy and rice is al dente, stir in cottage cheese and shredded mozzarella. Stir until cheeses are melted and incorporated.
Stir in cooked chicken and chopped fresh basil. Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Berenjenas Rellenas con Frijoles y Elote
recipes.visual_description: Two roasted eggplant halves, deeply caramelized, are centered on a round white ceramic plate. Each eggplant is generously filled with a vibrant mixture of dark black beans, bright yellow corn kernels, and diced red bell pepper. The filling is topped with a layer of lightly melted, crusted queso fresco, showing golden-brown spots. A generous sprinkle of fresh, bright green chopped cilantro covers the cheese. Beside the eggplant, a fresh lime wedge adds a pop of green. The overall presentation is rustic yet refined, showcasing natural textures and colors. The plate rests on a simple wooden table. A folded cotton napkin and a few corn tortillas are placed nearby, honoring traditional Mexican serving.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas for scooping.
Offer a side of authentic salsa roja or salsa verde.
Provide Mexican crema or sour cream for drizzling.

ingredients.name: Cooked black beans, rinsed and drained
Crumbled queso fresco or cotija cheese

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Halve eggplants lengthwise. Scoop out flesh, leaving a 1 cm border. Chop scooped eggplant flesh into small cubes.
Brush eggplant shells with 5 ml olive oil. Season with salt and pepper. Place cut-side up on a baking sheet. Roast for 15 minutes, until slightly tender.
Heat remaining 10 ml olive oil in a large pan over medium heat. Add diced onion and bell pepper. Sauté 5 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic and chopped eggplant flesh to the pan. Cook 7-8 minutes, stirring occasionally, until eggplant is tender.
Stir in black beans, corn kernels, diced tomato, minced chipotle, cumin, and Mexican oregano. Cook 5 minutes, allowing flavors to meld. Season with salt and pepper.
Remove roasted eggplant shells from oven. Spoon the bean and corn filling generously into each eggplant shell.
Top each stuffed eggplant half with crumbled queso fresco.
Return stuffed eggplants to the oven. Bake 15-20 minutes, until cheese is melted and lightly golden.
Garnish generously with fresh chopped cilantro. Serve immediately with lime wedges.
traditional_techniques: Roasting vegetables for smoky flavor and texture.
Sofrito base for the filling, building flavor layers.

recipes.recipe_name: Spanish Roasted Chicken with Paprika Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean, rustic white ceramic plate, showcasing a single generous portion. A golden-brown, crisply roasted chicken thigh, its skin slightly puckered and glistening, anchors the composition. Alongside the chicken are irregularly shaped, roasted potato chunks, their surfaces golden with hints of paprika, some edges slightly crisped. Interspersed among the potatoes are soft, deeply caramelized onion strands, their rich amber color providing a warm contrast. A scattering of vibrant green, freshly chopped flat-leaf parsley is sprinkled over the chicken and potatoes, adding a burst of color and freshness. The chicken is presented as a whole piece. The arrangement is natural and inviting, with moderate negative space on the plate. The background features a simple, light wooden table surface, a plain cotton napkin, and a sturdy, traditional fork and knife. Lighting is even and natural, enhancing the warmth of the dish.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread to sop up the pan juices.
Serve with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and vinegar.
Serve with a glass of dry Spanish white wine or a light red.

ingredients.name: Potatoes (e.g., Yukon Gold or Russet), medium

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Peel potatoes. Cut into 2-3 cm chunks.
Peel onions. Halve, then slice thinly.
Peel and finely mince garlic.
Heat 30ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs skin-side down for 6-8 minutes until golden brown and crispy. Flip chicken. Sear for 2-3 minutes on the other side. Remove chicken from skillet.
Add remaining 30ml olive oil to the skillet. Add sliced onions. Sauté over medium heat for 10-12 minutes until softened and caramelized.
Add minced garlic and smoked paprika to onions. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Deglaze skillet with white wine, if using. Scrape up any browned bits. Reduce by half.
Add chicken broth to the skillet. Bring to a simmer.
Add potato chunks to the skillet with the onion mixture. Stir to coat.
Nestle seared chicken thighs among the potatoes and onions in the skillet, skin-side up.
Transfer skillet to preheated oven. Roast for 25-30 minutes, or until chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C and potatoes are tender.
Remove from oven. Rest for 5 minutes.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley. Serve directly from the skillet or transfer to serving plates.
notes: Adjust paprika quantity to personal preference for smokiness or heat.
Bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs provide best flavor and moisture.
Ensure potatoes are cut uniformly for even cooking.

recipes.recipe_name: Italian Savory Egg and Cheese Bake
recipes.visual_description: A generous, rustic slice of Italian Savory Egg and Cheese Bake is presented on a simple, round, off-white ceramic plate. The dish showcases distinct layers: golden-brown cubed bread, creamy baked egg, vibrant red sliced tomatoes, and melted, bubbling mozzarella cheese, interspersed with tender, diced sautéed onion. The top is lightly browned and slightly puffed from baking, with fresh green basil leaves scattered casually over it. The slice reveals a soft, cohesive interior contrasting with subtly crisp edges. The plate rests on a warm, well-worn wooden kitchen table, beside a casually folded, red and white checkered cloth napkin. A fork with a slightly worn wooden handle is placed beside the plate. Natural, warm light illuminates the scene, highlighting the comforting textures and colors.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and red wine vinegar
Offer alongside a basket of crusty Italian bread
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C. Grease a 20x30 cm baking dish with butter.
Cut stale rustic bread into 2-3 cm cubes. Set aside.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add diced onion. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic to the skillet. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant. Remove from heat.
In a large bowl, whisk eggs, milk, salt, and black pepper until well combined.
Layer half of the cubed bread in the prepared baking dish.
Distribute half of the sautéed onion and garlic mixture over the bread.
Arrange half of the sliced tomatoes over the onion layer.
Sprinkle half of the shredded mozzarella and half of the grated Parmesan cheese over the tomatoes.
Repeat the layers with the remaining bread, onion-garlic mixture, tomatoes, and cheeses.
Pour the egg and milk mixture evenly over the layers, ensuring all bread is moistened. Gently press down with a spatula if needed.
Bake for 35-45 minutes, or until the top is golden brown and the egg mixture is set. A knife inserted into the center should come out clean.
Remove from oven. Let rest for 5 minutes.
Garnish with fresh chopped basil before serving.
notes: Using stale bread is crucial for this dish; it absorbs the egg mixture better without becoming soggy.

recipes.recipe_name: Медленное Тушеное Мясное Рагу с Паппарделле
recipes.visual_description: Одна порция насыщенного, деревенского Медленного Тушеного Мясного Рагу с Паппарделле подается на чистой белой фарфоровой тарелке. Широкие плоские макароны паппарделле щедро покрыты густым, кирпично-красным томатным рагу с говядиной. Видны крупные, неправильной формы куски нежной, разорванной говядины, демонстрирующие ее медленно приготовленную текстуру. Соус имеет глянцевый блеск, обволакивая пасту. Сверху блюдо посыпано ярко-зеленой свежей рубленой итальянской петрушкой и обильно присыпано мелко натертым бледно-желтым сыром пармезан, что добавляет ярких красок и текстуры. Тарелка хорошо сбалансирована с умеренным негативным пространством, подчеркивая уютный и сытный характер блюда. Обстановка включает простую деревянную поверхность стола с льняной салфеткой и вилкой рядом с тарелкой, все залито естественным, равномерным освещением на фоне ресторанного интерьера.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Подавать немедленно, горячим.
Предложить дополнительный тертый пармезан на столе.
Подавать с хрустящим деревенским хлебом для макания в соус.
instructions: Обсушите куски говядины. Приправьте солью и перцем.
В большой чугунной кастрюле или голландской печи нагрейте оливковое масло на среднем огне. Обжарьте говядину до золотистой корочки со всех сторон. Выньте говядину из кастрюли.
Уменьшите огонь до среднего. Добавьте нарезанные лук, морковь и сельдерей. Готовьте 8-10 минут, пока овощи не станут мягкими.
Добавьте измельченный чеснок и томатную пасту. Готовьте 2 минуты, постоянно помешивая.
Влейте красное вино. Доведите до кипения. Готовьте 3-5 минут, соскребая приставшие кусочки со дна кастрюли.
Верните говядину в кастрюлю. Добавьте измельченные помидоры, говяжий бульон, розмарин, тимьян и лавровый лист.
Доведите до кипения. Уменьшите огонь до минимума. Накройте крышкой. Тушите 2,5-3 часа, пока говядина не станет очень мягкой и легко разваливающейся.
Выньте говядину из рагу. Разорвите мясо вилкой на крупные куски. Удалите веточки трав и лавровый лист из соуса.
Верните мясо в соус. Перемешайте. Проверьте приправы.
Отварите паппарделле согласно инструкции на упаковке до состояния "аль денте".
Слейте воду с пасты. Добавьте пасту прямо в рагу. Перемешайте, чтобы паста полностью покрылась соусом.
notes: Рагу можно приготовить заранее и разогреть. Вкус станет только лучше.
Если соус слишком густой, добавьте немного воды от варки пасты.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Creamy Mushroom and Pea Sauce
recipes.visual_description: A golden-brown pan-seared chicken breast, presented whole or as two thick diagonal slices, is centered on a clean white porcelain plate. A rich, light cream sauce generously coats the chicken and pools around it, showcasing earthy brown sliced cremini mushrooms and vibrant green peas. Fresh coriander sprigs garnish the dish, adding a pop of green. The plating is clean and professional, with moderate negative space. The setting features a simple wooden table, a white cotton napkin, and standard silver flatware. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and colors against a subtly blurred bistro-style background.
instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season generously with salt and black pepper on both sides.

Heat olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Add chicken breasts. Sear for 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown. Internal temperature must reach 75°C. Remove chicken from pan. Set aside on a plate, cover loosely with foil.
Reduce heat to medium. Add butter to the same pan. Add diced shallot and cook for 2 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add sliced mushrooms to the pan. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until mushrooms release their liquid and turn golden.
Pour in chicken stock. Bring to a simmer. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan. Reduce liquid by half, about 3-4 minutes.
Stir in heavy cream and frozen green peas. Bring to a gentle simmer. Cook for 2-3 minutes until sauce slightly thickens and peas are heated through.
Return chicken breasts to the pan with the sauce. Cook for 1-2 minutes, spooning sauce over chicken, ensuring chicken is heated through.
Stir in chopped fresh coriander. Taste and adjust seasoning if needed.
notes: Serve immediately with a side of creamy mashed potatoes or steamed rice to absorb the delicious sauce.

recipes.recipe_name: Estofado de Ternera con Tomate y Patatas
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Estofado de Ternera con Tomate y Patatas is presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate. Large, irregular chunks of dark, rich braised beef, boasting a tender, fall-apart texture, are centrally arranged. Golden-brown roasted potato wedges, with slightly crisp exteriors and fluffy interiors, are artfully scattered around the beef. A generous, glossy, deep red tomato and paprika sauce pools around the beef and potatoes, adhering to their surfaces. The sauce is thick and rustic, with visible pieces of softened onion and fresh diced tomato. A vibrant sprinkle of finely chopped fresh parsley provides a contrasting pop of bright green. The plate rests on a simple, light wooden table surface, accompanied by a folded white cotton napkin and a fork. Natural, soft, even lighting illuminates the dish, creating a warm and inviting bistro atmosphere in the background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread (pan de pueblo) to soak up the rich sauce.
Pair with a glass of dry Spanish red wine, such as Rioja or Ribera del Duero.
instructions: Cut beef chuck into 4-5 cm chunks. Pat dry. Season beef generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat. Sear beef chunks on all sides until well browned. Do this in batches to avoid overcrowding. Remove beef and set aside.
Dice the onion. Add onion to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Mince garlic. Add garlic to the pot. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in red wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Reduce wine by half, about 3 minutes.
Add crushed tomatoes, beef broth, smoked paprika, and bay leaf. Bring to a simmer.
Return seared beef to the pot. Ensure beef is mostly submerged in the liquid. Cover the pot. Reduce heat to low.
Simmer for 2.5 to 3 hours, or until beef is fork-tender. Stir occasionally.
Preheat oven to 200°C (390°F).
Cut new potatoes into wedges. Toss with a drizzle of olive oil, salt, and pepper on a baking sheet.
Roast potatoes for 25-30 minutes, turning halfway, until golden brown and tender.
Dice fresh ripe tomatoes. Stir into the braising liquid during the last 15 minutes of cooking.
Remove bay leaf. Taste the sauce and adjust seasoning as needed.
Chop fresh parsley. Garnish braised beef and potatoes with chopped parsley before serving.
notes: For best flavor, braise the beef the day before and gently reheat. Flavors deepen overnight.
Adjust the consistency of the sauce by simmering longer for a thicker sauce, or adding a splash of broth for a thinner one.

recipes.recipe_name: Orecchiette with Italian Sausage and Broccoli Rabe
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented in a clean, white porcelain pasta bowl on a rustic wooden table. Orecchiette pasta shells are tossed with 3cm irregular chunks of seared Italian sausage and vibrant green broccoli rabe florets. Small wedges of red bell pepper and sliced cremini mushrooms provide color contrast. Julienned sun-dried tomatoes add flecks of deep crimson. The sauce is a light, translucent emulsion of olive oil and garlic, coating each ingredient with a gentle sheen. A dusting of coarse, golden-brown toasted breadcrumbs and fresh oregano leaves is concentrated in the center. The arrangement is natural and organic, showing balanced portions with visible negative space around the inner rim of the bowl.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a glass of Primitivo or Negroamaro wine
Provide extra virgin olive oil for drizzling at the table
Accompany with crusty sourdough bread
instructions: Bring 4 liters of heavily salted water to a boil.
Blanch broccoli rabe for 2 minutes until bright green. Remove and shock in ice water. Drain and chop into 5cm pieces.
Heat 20ml olive oil in a pan. Add breadcrumbs and half the oregano. Toast until golden and crisp. Set aside.
In a large skillet, heat 20ml olive oil over medium-high heat. Break sausage into 3cm chunks and sear until browned.
Add mushrooms and bell peppers to the skillet. Sauté for 6 minutes until softened.
Stir in garlic, sun-dried tomatoes, and chili flakes. Cook for 2 minutes.
Boil orecchiette in the same water used for broccoli rabe until al dente.
Reserve 150ml of pasta water. Drain pasta.
Add pasta and broccoli rabe to the skillet. Pour in reserved pasta water and remaining olive oil.
Toss vigorously over high heat for 1 minute to emulsify the sauce.
Season with salt and remaining oregano.
Divide into four bowls and top with toasted breadcrumbs.
notes: Do not overcook the broccoli rabe during the blanching stage to maintain its snap
Use high-quality bronze-die pasta for better sauce adhesion

recipes.recipe_name: Multicooker Mediterranean Chicken and Pasta
recipes.special_requests: Mediterranean cuisine, Not junk-food, recipe for multicook
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented in a shallow, rustic ceramic bowl, deep blue or earthy green. A generous, homely portion of tender chicken chunks, cut into irregular 3cm pieces, is intertwined with al dente short pasta. The pasta is coated in a rich, reddish-orange tomato sauce, infused with aromatic rosemary and garlic. Vibrant green wilted spinach leaves are interspersed. A scattering of golden-brown toasted pine nuts rests on top, providing textural interest. The bowl sits on a well-used wooden dining table. A simple, textured linen napkin is casually placed beside it. A few fresh rosemary sprigs and extra toasted pine nuts are nearby. The lighting is warm and natural, highlighting the food's inviting textures and colors. A single, traditional metal fork rests on the napkin.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread (e.g., ciabatta) for dipping in the sauce.
Offer a simple green salad with a lemon-oregano vinaigrette on the side.
Serve with a glass of dry white wine or still water.
instructions: Cut chicken thighs into 3cm chunks. Season with salt and pepper.
Set multicooker to "Sauté" mode. Add olive oil.
Brown chicken chunks for 3-4 minutes. Remove chicken.
Add minced garlic and chopped rosemary to the pot. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in diced tomatoes and chicken broth. Scrape bottom of pot to deglaze.
Add pasta to the liquid. Stir to submerge.
Return chicken to the pot. Do not stir extensively after adding pasta.
Close multicooker lid. Set to "Pressure Cook" or "Manual" for 5 minutes on high pressure.
Once cooking finishes, perform a quick release of pressure.
Open lid. Stir in fresh spinach until wilted.
Stir in toasted pine nuts.
Taste and adjust seasoning. Serve immediately.
notes: Adjust pasta cooking time based on your multicooker and pasta type. A general rule is half the box cooking time for al dente pressure cooking.
Ensure enough liquid to cover pasta for even cooking.
For an extra bright flavor, stir in a squeeze of fresh lemon juice at the end.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Creamy Bacon Mushroom Sauce
recipes.visual_description: A single pan-seared chicken breast, golden-brown and tender, is centrally placed on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. A generous portion of creamy, rich mushroom and bacon sauce is spooned artfully over and around the chicken. The sauce is off-white with visible dark brown sliced mushrooms and crispy, reddish-brown diced bacon pieces. The chicken shows a beautiful sear mark. A sprinkle of vibrant green chopped fresh parsley garnishes the top of the chicken and sauce, adding a pop of color. The plate is positioned on a simple, light-colored wooden table surface. A neatly folded white cotton napkin and standard silver flatware (fork and knife) are placed beside the plate. Natural, soft, even lighting illuminates the dish, creating subtle shadows and highlighting textures. The background is a slightly blurred, casual bistro setting. The entire plate is visible with appropriate negative space, showcasing a refined yet approachable presentation.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with creamy mashed potatoes or steamed rice.
Offer a side of simple green salad with a light vinaigrette.
Provide crusty bread for dipping in the sauce.
instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.

Heat 1 tablespoon olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken breasts for 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C). Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside.
Add diced bacon to the same skillet. Cook over medium heat until crispy. Remove bacon with a slotted spoon. Set aside. Leave rendered bacon fat in the skillet.
Add remaining 1 tablespoon olive oil to the skillet if needed. Add diced onion and sliced mushrooms. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened and browned.
Add minced garlic. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in chicken broth. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the skillet. Bring to a simmer.
Stir in heavy cream. Reduce heat to low. Simmer for 5 minutes, or until sauce slightly thickens. Season sauce with salt and pepper to taste.
Return cooked chicken breasts and cooked bacon to the skillet. Spoon sauce over chicken. Heat gently for 1-2 minutes.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley before serving.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
Adjust sauce consistency by simmering longer for a thicker sauce, or adding a splash more broth for a thinner sauce.

recipes.recipe_name: Spanish Chicken and Potato Croquettes with Spicy Tomato Relish
recipes.visual_description: A single starter portion of Spanish Chicken and Potato Croquettes is elegantly presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate, centrally placed on a simple wooden table. Three golden-brown, elongated croquettes are arranged neatly, slightly overlapping, their crisp, textured breadcrumb coating visible. A vibrant mound of chunky, deep red spicy tomato relish is spooned beside them, showcasing diced tomatoes and flecks of green chili. Fresh, finely chopped parsley garnishes the relish, adding a pop of color. A slice of lightly toasted, crusty white bread rests to the side. The setting includes a folded white cotton napkin and classic flatware. Natural, even lighting highlights the warm tones of the croquettes and rich relish. The background features a subtle, out-of-focus modern bistro ambiance, creating moderate negative space on the plate.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve as part of a tapas spread.
Accompany with additional crusty bread for dipping.
instructions: Cook chicken breast. Shred finely. Boil potatoes until tender. Mash well.
Heat butter in a pan. Sauté 1 diced onion until soft. Add 2 minced garlic cloves. Cook 1 minute.
Stir in flour. Cook 1 minute, stirring constantly, to form a roux.
Gradually whisk in milk until smooth and thick béchamel forms. Cook 2-3 minutes.
Stir in shredded chicken, mashed potatoes, salt, pepper, and nutmeg. Mix well.
Transfer mixture to a shallow dish. Cover with cling film touching surface. Chill 2 hours or until firm.
Shape chilled mixture into small oval or cylindrical croquettes (approx. 30g each).
Set up breading station: one bowl with beaten eggs, one with breadcrumbs.
Dip each croquette in egg, then roll in breadcrumbs, ensuring full coating.
Heat vegetable oil in a deep pot to 170°C.
Fry croquettes in batches until golden brown and crispy. Drain on paper towels. Cook chicken to 75°C (167°F).
For the relish: Heat olive oil in a small saucepan. Sauté 1 diced onion until soft.
Add 2 minced garlic cloves and chopped red chili. Cook 1 minute.
Add diced tomatoes, white wine vinegar, and sugar.
Simmer 10-15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until tomatoes break down and relish thickens.
Season with salt and pepper.
Plate 3-4 croquettes with a dollop of relish. Garnish with chopped parsley. Serve with toasted crusty bread.
notes: Croquettes can be prepared ahead of time and fried just before serving.
Ensure the croquette mixture is well chilled for easier shaping.
traditional_techniques: Making a béchamel sauce base for croquettes
Sofrito base for the tomato relish

recipes.recipe_name: Thai Green Curry with Kale and Edamame
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant Thai Green Curry with plant-based ingredients is presented in a deep, pristine white porcelain bowl. The creamy, aromatic green sauce envelops golden-brown pan-seared tofu cubes, tender-crisp, roughly chopped kale leaves, and bright green edamame. Thin red chili slices and fresh cilantro leaves are scattered across the top as a fresh garnish, adding pops of color. A lime wedge rests on the rim of the bowl, ready to be squeezed. Adjacent to the curry, a smaller, matching white porcelain bowl holds a perfectly mounded portion of fluffy white jasmine rice. Chopsticks are neatly placed across the rice bowl. The scene is set on a simple, light wooden table surface, with a folded cotton napkin beside the bowls. Natural, soft lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its rich textures and inviting colors.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately with a side of steamed jasmine rice.
Offer additional lime wedges for guests to squeeze over their curry.
Provide small bowls of chili flakes or a mild chili oil for extra heat.
instructions: Press tofu for 15 minutes to remove excess water. Cut into 2cm cubes.
Heat cooking oil in a large pot or wok over medium heat. Add diced shallot and minced garlic. Sauté for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Add grated ginger and green curry paste. Cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly, until aromatic.
Pour in coconut milk and vegetable broth. Stir well to combine. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Add tofu cubes to the simmering curry. Cook for 5-7 minutes, allowing tofu to absorb flavors.
Add kale (stems removed, roughly chopped) and edamame. Cook for another 3-5 minutes, until kale is tender-crisp and edamame is heated through.
Stir in soy sauce and brown sugar. Adjust seasoning to taste. Squeeze in fresh lime juice.
Remove from heat. Garnish with thin slices of red chili and fresh cilantro leaves. Serve hot.
notes: Adjust the amount of green curry paste to your preferred spice level.
For extra protein, lightly pan-fry the tofu cubes until golden before adding to the curry.
traditional_techniques: Balancing the five core Thai flavors (spicy, sour, sweet, salty, umami)
Sautéing curry paste to release aromatics

recipes.recipe_name: Savory Baked Pasta Cups
recipes.visual_description: Individual savory baked pasta cups are presented on a rustic wooden board. Each cup is golden-brown on top, with visible flecks of green herbs and melted cheese, showcasing a crisp exterior and a tender, creamy interior. The cups are perfectly portioned, filled with orzo pasta, diced crispy pancetta, and finely minced shallots. A light sprinkle of fresh chives garnishes the tops. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a simple wooden table and clean white porcelain dinner plates. Natural, even lighting highlights the inviting warmth and texture of the snack. A folded off-white cotton napkin rests beside the board, maintaining a clean, professional, yet approachable aesthetic. The dish is designed for relaxed, casual sharing.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Ideal for an Italian-style aperitivo or as a sophisticated finger food at gatherings.
Serve with a side of simple tomato confit or a light roasted red pepper aioli for dipping.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C (350°F). Lightly grease a 12-cup muffin tin.
Cook orzo pasta according to package directions until al dente. Drain well.
In a large skillet, cook diced pancetta over medium heat until crisp. Remove pancetta with a slotted spoon; set aside. Leave rendered fat in skillet.
Add finely diced shallot to the skillet. Sauté for 3 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant. Remove from heat.
In a large bowl, whisk eggs, heavy cream, and milk until combined. Stir in grated Parmesan, grated Fontina/Gruyere, chopped parsley, chopped chives, salt, and black pepper.
Add cooked orzo, crispy pancetta, and sautéed shallot-garlic mixture to the egg mixture. Stir gently to combine.
Spoon the mixture evenly into the prepared muffin tin cups. Fill each cup almost to the top.
Bake for 20-25 minutes, or until the cups are golden brown and set. A toothpick inserted into the center should come out clean.
Let cool in the muffin tin for 5 minutes before carefully removing. Serve warm or at room temperature.

recipes.recipe_name: Lomo Saltado
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Lomo Saltado presented on a clean white porcelain plate. The dish features 3cm chunks of seared beef sirloin with a deep brown crust. These are mixed with thick, glossy wedges of purple red onion and bright red Roma tomatoes. Golden, thick-cut potato batons are scattered through the beef mixture, all coated in a dark, shimmering sauce. A neat, molded dome of fluffy white rice sits on the side of the plate. Fresh green cilantro leaves garnish the top. The scene is set on a light wooden bistro table with a white cotton napkin and a small side bowl of spicy green aji sauce. The lighting is natural and even.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of Aji Verde (green chili sauce)
Accompany with Inca Kola or a glass of red wine
Traditionally eaten with both rice and potatoes in the same meal

ingredients.name: Red onions, cut into thick wedges
Roma tomatoes, cut into thick wedges

instructions: Season beef chunks with salt and pepper.
Heat 2 tablespoons of oil in a wok over high heat until smoking.
Sear beef in batches until browned and medium-rare.
Remove beef from wok and set aside.
Add remaining oil to the wok.
Stir-fry onion wedges for 2 minutes until slightly charred but crisp.
Add garlic and aji amarillo paste. Stir for 30 seconds.
Return beef to the wok.
Pour in soy sauce and red wine vinegar. Toss quickly.
Add tomato wedges. Stir for 30 seconds to warm through.
Fold in the cooked potato fries and half the cilantro.
Remove from heat immediately.
Serve with white rice.
notes: Ensure the wok is extremely hot before adding beef to achieve a smoky flavor.
Do not overcook the tomatoes; they should be warm but hold their shape.
The potatoes should be added at the very last second to maintain some crispness.

recipes.recipe_name: French Mustard Chicken with Roasted Garlic Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of French Mustard Chicken is presented on a round, clean white porcelain dinner plate, showcasing a golden-brown, seared bone-in chicken thigh, its skin crisp. The chicken rests in a rich, creamy Dijon mustard sauce, glistening under natural, even lighting. Beside the chicken, a generous cluster of roasted potato chunks, their skins slightly browned and interiors tender, are intermingled with vibrant, blistered cherry tomato halves and soft, caramelized garlic slices. The arrangement is organic yet composed, with moderate negative space. A scattering of fresh, bright green chopped tarragon and parsley garnishes the dish, providing a pop of color and freshness. The plate sits on a simple, light-colored wooden table surface. A neatly folded white cotton napkin is placed to the side. The background hints at a modern bistro setting, clean and unfussy, allowing the dish to be the focal point.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a fresh, crusty baguette to soak up the rich sauce.
Accompany with a simple green salad dressed with a light vinaigrette.

ingredients.name: Cherry tomatoes or small plum tomatoes

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.

Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large oven-safe pan or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear chicken thighs skin-side down for 8-10 minutes until golden brown and crisp. Flip and sear for 2-3 minutes on the other side. Remove chicken from pan. Set aside.
Peel and thinly slice shallots. Mince 3 garlic cloves.
Add remaining 15 ml olive oil to the same pan. Sauté sliced shallots for 2-3 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Deglaze pan with white wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom. Simmer for 2 minutes until wine slightly reduces.
Stir in Dijon mustard and chicken stock. Bring to a simmer. Return chicken thighs to the pan, skin-side up.
Cover pan. Transfer to preheated oven. Cook for 20 minutes.
While chicken cooks, prepare potatoes and tomatoes. Wash potatoes. Cut larger potatoes into 2-3 cm chunks. Halve cherry tomatoes. Slice remaining 3 garlic cloves.

Toss potatoes, tomatoes, and sliced garlic with a drizzle of olive oil, salt, and pepper on a baking tray. Roast in the oven for 25-30 minutes, or until potatoes are tender and golden. Tomatoes should be slightly burst.

Remove chicken from oven. Stir in heavy cream, chopped tarragon, and half of the chopped parsley into the pan sauce. Simmer gently on stovetop for 5 minutes until sauce slightly thickens. Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C.

To serve, place a chicken thigh on each plate. Spoon generous amount of mustard sauce over chicken. Arrange roasted garlic potatoes and tomatoes beside the chicken. Garnish with remaining fresh parsley.
notes: Bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs provide the best flavor and moisture for this dish.
Adjust mustard quantity to your preferred level of tanginess.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Bacon and Caramelized Onion Tagliatelle
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, showcasing a generous portion of golden-hued tagliatelle. The pasta is coated in a rich, creamy sauce, subtly speckled with translucent, deeply caramelized onion strands. Scattered throughout are crisp, golden-brown chunks of pan-fried bacon. A vibrant sprinkle of fresh, finely chopped green parsley provides a contrasting pop of color on top. The dish has a natural, flowing arrangement, with the pasta forming a soft mound, allowing for moderate negative space on the plate. The textures are varied: smooth pasta, soft onions, and crunchy bacon. The overall presentation is inviting and professional, with a focus on the appealing colors and textures of the ingredients. A simple cotton napkin rests beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish.
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large pan over medium heat. Add diced bacon. Cook until crispy.
Remove bacon with a slotted spoon. Set aside. Leave rendered fat in the pan.
Add thinly sliced onions to the pan with bacon fat. Cook over medium-low heat for 15-20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until deeply caramelized and soft.
Add minced garlic to the pan with onions. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Deglaze the pan with broth, scraping up any browned bits.
Pour in heavy cream. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Cook tagliatelle according to package directions in salted boiling water until al dente. Reserve 120ml pasta water before draining.
Add cooked tagliatelle to the pan with the cream sauce. Add half of the crispy bacon and half of the grated Parmesan.
Toss well to coat pasta. Add reserved pasta water as needed to achieve desired creamy consistency.
Season with salt and black pepper.
Serve immediately. Garnish each portion with remaining crispy bacon, grated Parmesan, and fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Coconut Green Curry with Crispy Tofu, Kale, and Edamame
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented in a deep, pristine white porcelain bowl, showcasing a vibrant, creamy green curry. Roughly chopped tender kale leaves and bright green shelled edamame are generously dispersed throughout the rich, aromatic sauce. Golden-brown, crispy 2cm tofu cubes are artfully arranged on top, providing textural contrast. The curry's color is a lush, inviting green, accented by the white of the coconut milk and the golden hue of the tofu. A scattering of thinly sliced fresh red chili and bright green cilantro leaves garnishes the dish. A small, separate white bowl of fluffy steamed jasmine rice sits beside it, with simple wooden chopsticks resting nearby. The composition is balanced, with moderate negative space, presented on a simple wooden table under natural, even lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Steamed jasmine rice
Fresh lime wedges
Chopped cilantro
instructions: Press tofu block for 30 minutes to remove excess water. Cut into 2cm cubes.
Heat 30ml neutral oil in a large pan or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add tofu cubes. Cook, turning occasionally, until golden and crispy on all sides. Remove tofu. Set aside.
Add remaining 15ml oil to the same pan. Add finely chopped shallots and minced garlic. Sauté for 2 minutes until softened.
Add grated ginger and thinly sliced red chili. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in green curry paste. Cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly, to release aromas.
Pour in coconut milk and 250ml water. Bring the mixture to a gentle simmer, stirring well to combine.
Add roughly chopped kale and shelled edamame. Cook for 3-5 minutes, or until kale is tender-crisp and edamame are heated through.
Stir in fresh lime juice and lime zest. Season with maple syrup and salt to taste, adjusting sweetness and saltiness as needed.
Gently fold in the crispy tofu cubes. Heat through for 1 minute.
Serve immediately in deep bowls, accompanied by steamed jasmine rice.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Bacon and Caramelized Onion Pasta
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of Creamy Bacon and Caramelized Onion Pasta is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. The spaghetti is artfully intertwined, coated in a rich, glossy, light golden-brown cream sauce. Small, crispy, deep golden-brown diced bacon pieces are scattered throughout and on top of the pasta. Soft, tender strands of deep amber caramelized onion are visibly integrated within the dish. Fresh, bright green chopped parsley is sprinkled over the pasta, adding a vibrant color contrast. The dish has a balanced composition with moderate negative space, showcasing the texture of the pasta and the varied colors of its ingredients. The plate rests on a simple wooden table surface. A neatly folded white cotton napkin is placed beside the plate. The scene is illuminated by soft, even natural light, creating a warm and inviting bistro atmosphere. A silver fork is placed to the side of the plate. The background is softly blurred, suggestive of a modern casual restaurant setting.
instructions: Cook pasta according to package directions until al dente. Drain, reserving 250ml of pasta water.
Heat olive oil in a large pan over medium heat. Add diced bacon. Cook until crispy. Remove bacon with a slotted spoon. Set aside. Leave rendered fat in the pan.
Add thinly sliced onions to the pan with bacon fat. Reduce heat to medium-low. Cook, stirring occasionally, for 30-40 minutes until deeply caramelized and soft.
Add minced garlic to the caramelized onions. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in heavy cream. Bring to a gentle simmer. Stir in grated Parmesan cheese until melted and smooth. Season with salt and black pepper.
Add cooked pasta to the sauce in the pan. Toss to coat evenly. Add reserved pasta water gradually, if needed, to achieve desired creamy consistency.
Stir in the crispy bacon pieces.
Serve immediately. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley and additional grated Parmesan cheese.

recipes.recipe_name: French Braised Beef with Root Vegetables
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of French braised beef, presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, centrally placed on a simple wooden bistro table. The rich, dark brown beef chunks, deeply caramelized and fork-tender, are nestled amongst vibrant roasted root vegetables: thick-cut carrot rounds, medium potato cubes, and pearl onions, all coated in a glossy, dark red wine reduction. Fresh button mushrooms, halved and sautéed, are interspersed throughout. A sprinkle of freshly chopped flat-leaf parsley adds a bright green contrast. The arrangement is organic and inviting, with moderate negative space around the edges of the plate. A folded white cotton napkin and classic silver flatware are placed beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish from above, highlighting its rich textures and inviting warmth.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty baguette slices for dipping in the sauce.
Pair with a simple green salad dressed with a light vinaigrette.
instructions: Preheat oven to 160°C.
Pat beef chuck dry. Cut into large 5cm chunks. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear beef chunks on all sides until deeply browned. Remove beef from pot.
Add carrots cut into thick rounds, onions cut into wedges, and celery cut into thick slices to the pot. Sauté 8-10 minutes until softened and lightly browned.
Stir in minced garlic and tomato paste. Cook 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Deglaze pot with red wine, scraping up all browned bits from the bottom. Reduce wine by half.
Return beef to the pot. Add beef stock, thyme sprigs, and bay leaf. Liquid should mostly cover the beef.
Bring mixture to a simmer. Cover the Dutch oven tightly.
Transfer Dutch oven to the preheated oven. Braise for 2.5-3 hours, or until beef is very tender.
Add potatoes cut into medium cubes and mushrooms halved to the pot. Continue braising for another 30-45 minutes, until vegetables are tender.
Remove thyme sprigs and bay leaf before serving.
Taste and adjust seasoning as needed.
Serve hot.
notes: Ensure beef is fork-tender before serving for best results.

recipes.recipe_name: Coastal Crab Pita Flatbreads
recipes.visual_description: A single individual portion of a Coastal Crab Pita Flatbread is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. The pita, golden and slightly crisped from baking, is cut into two large halves, showcasing its appealing texture. A creamy, herb-infused base peeks from beneath generous, tender chunks of white lump crab meat. Vibrant red halves of cherry tomatoes and delicate, thinly sliced red onion rings are scattered across the top. Melted, bubbly mozzarella and crumbled feta create a tempting cheesy layer. The entire flatbread is garnished with a fresh sprinkle of finely chopped green dill and chives, and a hint of red pepper flakes adds a subtle color pop. The plate rests on a simple wooden table surface, with a neatly folded cotton napkin positioned beside it. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its fresh ingredients and inviting textures. The background is a soft, unobtrusive blur of a casual restaurant setting.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (390°F).
In a small bowl, combine softened cream cheese, half of the chopped dill, half of the chopped chives, minced garlic, lemon zest, 15 ml olive oil, salt, and black pepper. Mix well.
Lay pita breads on a baking sheet. Lightly brush each pita with remaining 15 ml olive oil.
Spread an even layer of the cream cheese mixture over each pita bread, leaving a small border.
Evenly distribute the lump crab meat over the cream cheese base.
Arrange thinly sliced red onion and halved cherry tomatoes over the crab.
Sprinkle shredded mozzarella and crumbled feta cheeses over the toppings.
Bake for 10-12 minutes, or until the pita edges are golden and the cheese is melted and bubbly.
Remove from oven. Garnish each flatbread with remaining fresh dill, chives, and a pinch of red pepper flakes.
Slice each flatbread into quarters or halves. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Bacon and Mushroom Risotto
recipes.visual_description: The Creamy Bacon and Mushroom Risotto is served in a shallow, clean white porcelain bowl. The risotto is fluid and free-flowing, presenting a rich, creamy texture with visible al dente rice grains. It has a warm, inviting golden-beige color. Scattered throughout are browned, savory mushroom slices and small, crispy chunks of bacon, adding contrasting deep browns and reddish-browns. A light sprinkle of vibrant green chopped fresh parsley provides a fresh color pop. The dish is garnished with a few extra crispy bacon pieces on top, showcasing their irregular, rustic shapes. The plating is organized but not rigid, allowing the risotto's natural flow. There is moderate negative space around the dish. The bowl sits on a simple wooden table surface with a folded white cotton napkin beside it. Natural, even lighting highlights the risotto's glossy texture.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a glass of dry white wine, such as Pinot Grigio.
Offer extra grated Parmigiano Reggiano at the table.
Serve with crusty Italian bread to sop up any extra sauce.
instructions: Cook diced bacon in a large, heavy-bottomed pot over medium heat until crispy. Remove bacon with a slotted spoon. Reserve 15 ml of bacon fat in the pot.

Add olive oil to the pot with bacon fat. Add diced onion. Sauté until translucent, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic and sliced mushrooms. Cook until mushrooms are tender and browned, about 5-7 minutes.
Add Arborio rice to the pot. Stir constantly for 2 minutes until grains are translucent at the edges.
Pour in white wine. Stir until completely absorbed.

Begin adding warm broth, one ladleful (about 120 ml) at a time. Stir frequently. Wait until each ladleful is almost fully absorbed before adding the next. Continue for 18-20 minutes, until rice is creamy and al dente.
Remove from heat. Stir in butter, grated Parmigiano Reggiano, and most of the crispy bacon. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Ladle risotto immediately into warm bowls. Garnish with remaining crispy bacon and fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Mediterranean Chicken & Orzo Soup
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of Mediterranean Chicken & Orzo Soup is presented in a deep, rustic ceramic bowl with natural, earthy tones. The rich, tomato-infused golden broth fills the bowl, studded with tender, shredded chunks of golden-brown chicken and small, al dente orzo pasta. Vibrant diced carrots, celery, and onion pieces are visible throughout, adding pops of natural color and texture. A scattering of golden-brown toasted pine nuts rests on the surface, along with bright green flecks of fresh chopped parsley. The soup appears hearty and comforting, with components touching naturally. The bowl sits on a well-worn wooden kitchen table, bathed in warm, soft natural light, suggesting a cozy, lived-in family dining atmosphere. A simple, casually folded linen napkin and a rustic metal spoon rest beside the bowl, enhancing the homely presentation.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty rustic bread for dipping.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Brown chicken thighs for 3-4 minutes per side. Remove chicken. Set aside.
Add diced onion, carrots, and celery to the pot. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in diced tomatoes, chicken broth, and rosemary sprigs. Bring to a boil.
Return browned chicken thighs to the pot. Reduce heat to low. Simmer for 20 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
Remove chicken from the pot. Shred chicken using two forks. Discard rosemary sprigs.
Increase heat to medium. Add orzo pasta to the simmering soup. Cook for 8-10 minutes, or until al dente.
Return shredded chicken to the pot. Stir well.
Season soup with salt and pepper to taste.
While pasta cooks, toast pine nuts in a dry small pan over medium-low heat for 2-3 minutes, until golden and fragrant. Watch carefully to prevent burning.
Ladle hot soup into individual bowls. Garnish each serving with toasted pine nuts and fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Beef Shank with Fermented Tomato Pasta & Crispy Root Skins
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Braised Beef Shank with Fermented Tomato Pasta is presented on a handcrafted ceramic plate in an earthy cream tone. The pasta, lightly coated in a vibrant reddish-orange fermented tomato-bell pepper sauce, forms a natural, unforced mound. A generous, irregularly shaped chunk of deeply browned, tender braised beef shank rests prominently atop the pasta. A scattering of golden-brown, irregularly shaped crispy root vegetable skins is artfully placed to add texture and visual interest. A few small, fresh green sprigs of parsley or basil provide a subtle color contrast. The entire plate is visible, with ample negative space around the dish. The setting features a light bamboo table surface, an undyed linen napkin in natural beige, and soft, natural lighting. The background is clean and minimalist, with a hint of natural elements like a potted herb plant.
instructions: Prepare fermented tomato-bell pepper sauce: Dice tomatoes and bell peppers. Combine with non-iodized salt (2% of vegetable weight) and non-chlorinated water in a clean jar. Ensure vegetables are submerged. Seal loosely. Ferment at room temperature for 5-7 days. Bubbling indicates fermentation. Blend fermented vegetables and brine into a smooth sauce. Strain if desired.

Prepare beef shank: Season beef shank chunks with salt and pepper. Heat 15ml olive oil in a heavy pot over medium-high heat. Sear beef chunks on all sides until deeply browned. Remove beef and set aside.

Braise beef: Add remaining 15ml olive oil to the pot. Sauté diced onion, carrots, and celery until softened, about 8 minutes. If using, deglaze with red wine, scraping up browned bits. Add beef stock. Bring to a simmer. Return beef chunks to the pot. Ensure beef is mostly submerged. Cover and braise in oven at 150°C (300°F) or on stovetop over low heat for 2.5-3 hours, or until beef is fork-tender. Remove beef. Reduce braising liquid by simmering until slightly thickened. Shred beef or keep as chunks.

Prepare crispy root skins: Thoroughly wash carrot, parsnip, and potato skins. Toss skins with a drizzle of olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread in a single layer on a baking sheet. Bake at 180°C (350°F) for 10-15 minutes, or until golden and crispy. Watch closely to prevent burning.
Cook pasta: Bring a large pot of salted water to a rolling boil. Add pasta and cook according to package directions until al dente. Reserve 120ml pasta cooking water before draining.

Assemble dish: Gently warm the fermented tomato-bell pepper sauce in a large pan. Add drained pasta and toss to coat. Add a splash of reserved pasta water if needed to reach desired consistency. Stir in shredded or chunked beef. Plate immediately. Top each portion with a braised beef shank chunk. Garnish with crispy root vegetable skins and a few fresh parsley or basil sprigs.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Tomato & Garlic Roast Chicken with Crispy Potato Skins
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Fermented Tomato & Garlic Roast Chicken is centrally placed on a handcrafted, matte cream-beige ceramic plate. One golden-brown, whole chicken thigh with crispy skin, glistening from the roast, anchors the dish. Rustic chunks of roasted potato, their skins slightly browned and interiors fluffy, are naturally scattered around the chicken. A few whole, caramelized garlic cloves and a sprig of fresh rosemary are nestled among the potatoes. A small pile of crispy, golden-brown potato skins, a zero-waste element, is positioned neatly beside the chicken. The color palette is earthy, featuring rich browns, subtle reds from the tomato marinade, and natural potato tones, accented by green herbs. The textures are varied: crisp chicken skin, tender chicken meat, soft potato, and crunchy potato skins. The plate is not overcrowded, allowing for ample negative space that emphasizes the minimalist, ingredient-focused presentation. The setting is an unpolished, light reclaimed wood table. An undyed linen napkin in natural beige is folded simply beside the plate. Soft, diffused natural light illuminates the scene from the side, creating gentle shadows and highlighting the food's natural textures. The background is clean and unobtrusive, featuring a hint of blurred green foliage, reinforcing the sustainable theme.
instructions: Prepare fermented tomato-garlic paste: Roughly chop 400g tomatoes and 8 cloves garlic. Blend with 10g sea salt until a coarse paste forms. Transfer to a clean jar. Cover loosely or use an airlock. Ferment at room temperature for 3-5 days until slightly tangy. Stir daily.
Pat chicken thighs dry. In a bowl, coat chicken with half of the fermented tomato-garlic paste. Marinate for at least 30 minutes, or up to 4 hours in the refrigerator.
Preheat oven to 200°C (390°F).
Wash potatoes thoroughly. Peel potatoes, reserving all peels. Cut peeled potatoes into rustic 3-4cm chunks.
In a large roasting pan, toss potato chunks with 15ml olive oil, remaining 5g sea salt, and black pepper. Add remaining garlic cloves (whole) and rosemary/thyme sprigs to the pan.
Arrange marinated chicken thighs skin-side up among the potatoes in the roasting pan.
Roast for 35-45 minutes. Chicken internal temperature must reach 75°C (167°F). Potatoes should be tender and lightly browned.

While chicken roasts, prepare crispy potato skins: In a separate bowl, toss reserved potato peels with remaining 15ml olive oil, a pinch of salt, and pepper. Spread peels in a single layer on a baking sheet.
Bake potato peels for 15-20 minutes, or until golden brown and crispy. If needed, bake during the last 15 minutes of chicken roasting or immediately after.
Remove chicken and potatoes from oven. Let chicken rest for 5 minutes before serving.
Serve individual portions of roast chicken and potatoes. Garnish each plate with crispy potato skins.
notes: To further reduce waste, save chicken bones and vegetable scraps to make a flavorful stock.
Any remaining fermented tomato-garlic paste can be stored in the refrigerator for up to 2 weeks and used as a flavor base for other dishes.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Coconut Cutlets
recipes.visual_description: The Spicy Coconut Cutlets are presented on a rustic, round ceramic plate with natural imperfections, placed on a well-used wooden dining table. Each cutlet is round and golden-brown, showcasing a crisp, pan-fried exterior and a rich, textured interior of shredded coconut and mashed potato. A subtle hint of green from finely chopped coriander is visible within the cutlet mixture. The cutlets are arranged casually, slightly overlapping, creating an inviting, homely feel. A small bowl of vibrant green mint-coriander chutney sits alongside, ready for dipping. A few fresh coriander sprigs are casually placed near the cutlets for a touch of fresh color. The scene is bathed in warm, soft kitchen lighting, evoking a comfortable family dining atmosphere. A simple cloth napkin is loosely draped nearby, completing the authentic Indian home setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of fresh mint-coriander chutney or tamarind chutney.
Accompanied by chai tea.
instructions: Boil potatoes until tender. Peel and mash them thoroughly.
In a large bowl, combine mashed potatoes, shredded coconut, chopped green chilies, grated ginger, minced garlic, clove powder, black pepper, maple syrup, chopped coriander, rice flour, and salt.
Mix all ingredients until a cohesive mixture forms.
Divide the mixture into 8 equal portions. Shape each portion into a flat, round cutlet.
Heat oil in a large frying pan over medium heat.
Place cutlets in the hot oil. Do not overcrowd the pan.
Pan-fry for 3-4 minutes per side, until golden brown and crisp.
Remove cutlets from pan. Drain on paper towels.
Serve hot.
notes: Adjust chili amount based on spice preference.
For a deeper flavor, lightly toast the shredded coconut before adding to the mixture.
Rice flour helps create a crispier exterior. Besan (chickpea flour) can be used as an alternative for binding.
traditional_techniques: Pan-frying until golden brown and crisp

recipes.recipe_name: Bacon and Caramelized Onion Risotto
recipes.visual_description: A single, refined portion of creamy, golden-hued risotto rests naturally on a clean, round white porcelain plate, its fluid consistency evident. The al dente Arborio rice is richly infused, showcasing finely diced, golden-brown caramelized onions throughout. A generous sprinkle of crispy, diced bacon pieces crowns the risotto, providing a textural contrast and savory visual highlight. Freshly chopped vibrant green parsley is scattered over the top, adding a pop of color and freshness. The dish is presented on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by standard European flatware and a folded cotton napkin placed beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, emphasizing its inviting textures and warm colors in a professional, approachable restaurant setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately while hot and fluid.
Offer crusty bread on the side for soaking up any extra sauce.
instructions: Prepare all ingredients. Dice bacon, finely dice onion, mince garlic. Heat chicken stock in a separate pot; keep it hot.

In a large, heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven, cook diced bacon over medium heat until crispy. Remove crispy bacon with a slotted spoon and set aside on paper towels. Leave rendered bacon fat in the pot.
Add olive oil to the pot with bacon fat. Add finely diced onion. Cook over medium-low heat for 8-10 minutes until deeply caramelized and tender, stirring occasionally.
Add minced garlic to the pot. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant. Do not brown the garlic.
Add Arborio rice to the pot. Stir constantly for 2 minutes to toast the rice until the edges become translucent.
Pour in the white wine. Stir constantly until the wine is completely absorbed by the rice.

Begin adding hot chicken stock, one ladleful (about 150ml) at a time. Stir continuously. Wait until each ladleful is almost fully absorbed before adding the next. Continue this process for 18-20 minutes until the rice is creamy and al dente (still has a slight bite). You may not need all the stock.
Remove the pot from heat. Stir in butter and grated Parmesan cheese vigorously. This process is called mantecatura, creating a creamy texture.
Season the risotto with salt and black pepper to taste. The consistency should be fluid and flowing, not stiff.
Serve the risotto immediately in warm bowls or plates. Garnish each portion with the reserved crispy bacon and freshly chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Vanilla Yogurt Mousse with Cherry Gelee and Apricot Confit
recipes.visual_description: Eight perfectly uniform, miniature cylindrical or cube-shaped petit fours are artfully arranged on a large, pristine white rectangular bone china platter. The plating features abundant negative space, with each petit four precisely positioned to create a minimalist yet elegant composition. Each petit four reveals distinct layers: a base of vibrant deep red cherry gelee, a delicate layer of pale orange apricot confit, and a dominant top layer of creamy, off-white vanilla yogurt mousse. A small, irregular sprinkle of golden-brown lemon sablé crumble surrounds the base of each petit four, providing a textural contrast. Each petit four is crowned with a single, tiny, bright green micro-mint leaf, providing a precise pop of color and freshness. The scene is set on a luxurious white Carrara marble surface. A crisp, white linen napkin, folded into a precise triangle, rests subtly in the background. Dramatic professional lighting creates soft shadows, enhancing the architectural precision and sophisticated simplicity of the dessert. The overall presentation is ultra-minimalist, showcasing the flawless execution and refined artistry of each component.
instructions: Prepare Lemon Sablé Crumble: Combine flour, cold butter, powdered sugar, lemon zest, and salt in a food processor. Pulse until coarse crumbs form. Press mixture onto a parchment-lined baking sheet. Chill 30 minutes. Bake at 160°C for 15-20 minutes until golden. Cool completely. Break into small, irregular crumbles.

Prepare Apricot Confit: Combine apricots, granulated sugar, and lemon juice in a small saucepan. Cook over medium-low heat for 10-15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until apricots are very tender and liquid is syrupy. Mash lightly with a fork or pulse briefly in a food processor for a chunky texture. Cool completely.

Prepare Cherry Gelee: Puree pitted cherries. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve to remove any skin or pulp. You need 150 ml cherry puree. Bloom 2 grams gelatin in ice water for 5 minutes. Heat cherry puree, 30 grams granulated sugar, and 10 ml lemon juice in a small saucepan until sugar dissolves. Squeeze excess water from gelatin. Stir gelatin into warm cherry mixture until fully dissolved. Pour a thin layer (approx. 5 mm) into the bottom of 8 small silicone cube or cylindrical molds (approx. 3x3x3 cm or 3 cm diameter x 3 cm height). Chill until set, about 30 minutes.

Prepare Vanilla Yogurt Mousse: Bloom 4 grams gelatin in ice water for 5 minutes. Gently warm 50 grams Greek yogurt with vanilla bean seeds and scraped pod over low heat until warm. Squeeze excess water from gelatin. Stir gelatin into warm yogurt until fully dissolved. Remove vanilla pod. Whisk remaining 200 grams cold Greek yogurt into the warm yogurt mixture until smooth. Whip heavy cream to soft peaks. Gently fold whipped cream into the yogurt mixture until just combined.

Assemble Petit Fours: Once cherry gelee is set in molds, pipe or spoon a thin layer of apricot confit over the gelee. Chill 10 minutes. Fill molds to the top with vanilla yogurt mousse. Tap molds gently to remove air bubbles. Freeze for at least 4 hours, or until completely firm.
Demold and Plate: Carefully demold the frozen petit fours. Allow to temper in the refrigerator for 15-20 minutes before serving.
Garnish and Serve: Arrange 8 petit fours artfully on a chilled serving platter. Garnish each petit four with a single micro-mint leaf and a sprinkle of lemon sablé crumble around the base.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Butternut Squash and Apple Soup with Ditalini
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of creamy Roasted Butternut Squash and Apple Soup is presented in a clean white porcelain bowl. The soup exhibits a warm, inviting orange hue, indicating its smooth, velvety texture. Small ditalini pasta shapes are visible, partially submerged within the rich liquid, providing a subtle textural contrast. A single, vibrant green fresh sage leaf is artfully placed on the soup's surface, offering a pop of color. A light, delicate dusting of finely grated Parmesan cheese lightly covers a section of the soup. The bowl rests on a simple wooden table surface. A neatly folded white cotton napkin is placed beside the bowl. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its fresh ingredients. The background is softly blurred, suggesting a modern bistro setting, keeping focus on the elegant, approachable presentation of the soup.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Peel and deseed squash. Cut into 2 cm cubes.
Core apples. Cut into 2 cm cubes.
Toss squash and apples with 15 ml olive oil and 4-5 sage leaves. Season with salt and pepper.
Roast 25-30 minutes until tender and lightly caramelized.
Heat remaining 15 ml olive oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add diced onion. Cook 5 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Add roasted squash, apples, and vegetable broth to pot. Bring to a simmer.
Simmer 10 minutes to combine flavors.
Carefully blend soup until smooth using an immersion blender or stand blender.
Return soup to pot. Stir in heavy cream if using. Keep warm.
In separate pot, cook ditalini according to package directions until al dente. Drain well.
Ladle hot soup into bowls. Add a spoonful of cooked ditalini to each bowl.
Garnish with a fresh sage leaf and a sprinkle of Parmesan.

recipes.recipe_name: Gochujang Pork Ragu with Pan-Seared Chicken, Calamari & Kimchi Pasta
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Gochujang Pork Ragu with Pan-Seared Chicken, Calamari & Kimchi Pasta is presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate, centrally composed with moderate negative space. A mound of al dente rigatoni, coated in a rich, reddish-brown Gochujang pork ragu, forms the base. Tender, shredded pork is visibly intertwined with the pasta and vibrant orange kimchi pieces. Thick, golden-brown pan-seared chicken chunks are nestled atop the ragu. Beside them, tender, opaque calamari rings and tentacles, with a slight char, add visual contrast.
