Prepare the Crispy Spinach: Heat neutral oil in a small saucepan to 170°C. Carefully add a few spinach leaves at a time. They will crisp quickly (10-15 seconds). Remove with a slotted spoon. Drain on paper towels. Season lightly with salt.

Cook and Plate: Bring a large pot of salted water to a rolling boil. Carefully add agnolotti. Cook for 2-3 minutes, or until al dente and floating. Using a slotted spoon, transfer 15-20 agnolotti per plate. Arrange agnolotti artfully on each warm plate, leaving abundant white space. Ladle a small amount (approx. 60-80ml) of warm smoked provolone brodo around the agnolotti. Drizzle a few drops of the vibrant broccoli rabe essence oil over the agnolotti and brodo. Garnish with 2-3 crispy spinach leaves. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Baked Jumbo Shells with Broccoli Rabe, Spinach, and Smoked Provolone
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of baked jumbo pasta shells is presented in a clean, white porcelain individual baking dish. Three to four generously stuffed shells are nestled in a vibrant red marinara sauce. The top of each shell features a bubbly, golden-brown crust of melted smoked provolone cheese, with glimpses of the creamy ricotta and tender green spinach and broccoli rabe filling peeking from the sides. The broccoli rabe is chopped into discernible 2-3 cm pieces. Fresh, bright green basil leaves are scattered artfully over the top, providing a color contrast. The dish sits on a simple wooden table surface in a modern bistro setting. A crisp white cotton napkin is folded beside the dish. Traditional Italian flatware (fork and spoon) rests next to the plate. The background is softly blurred, showing a casual restaurant atmosphere with natural, even lighting that highlights the food's textures and colors. The entire plate is visible, with moderate negative space. A small, white ramekin holding extra grated Parmesan cheese is placed nearby.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve hot with crusty Italian bread for dipping in the sauce.
Accompany with a simple green salad dressed with vinaigrette.
Offer extra grated Parmesan cheese at the table.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C (375°F).
Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Add jumbo pasta shells. Cook according to package directions until al dente. Drain. Rinse with cold water to prevent sticking. Set aside.

Wash broccoli rabe thoroughly. Trim tough ends. Blanch broccoli rabe in boiling water for 2 minutes. Immediately transfer to an ice bath to stop cooking. Drain well. Squeeze out excess water. Coarsely chop the blanched broccoli rabe into 2-3 cm pieces.

Heat olive oil in a large pan over medium heat. Add minced garlic and red pepper flakes. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant. Add chopped broccoli rabe. Sauté for 3-4 minutes. Add fresh spinach. Cook until spinach wilts completely. Remove from heat. Season with salt and pepper. Let cool slightly. Squeeze out any remaining liquid from the greens.

In a large bowl, combine ricotta cheese, 100 grams of shredded smoked provolone, and Parmesan cheese. Add the sautéed broccoli rabe and spinach mixture. Mix well. Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Spread 200 ml of marinara sauce evenly on the bottom of a 23x33 cm (9x13 inch) baking dish.
Carefully stuff each cooked pasta shell with the ricotta and greens mixture. Arrange stuffed shells in a single layer in the baking dish over the marinara sauce.
Pour the remaining marinara sauce over the stuffed shells. Sprinkle the remaining 50 grams of shredded smoked provolone cheese over the top.
Bake for 20-25 minutes, or until the sauce is bubbly and the cheese is melted and lightly golden. If desired, broil for the last 2 minutes for extra browning.
Remove from oven. Let rest for 5 minutes before serving. Garnish with fresh basil leaves.
notes: Ensure broccoli rabe and spinach are well-drained after blanching and sautéing to prevent a watery filling.
For best results, use whole milk ricotta for a richer, creamier filling.

recipes.recipe_name: Compressed Beef Terrine, Potato Pavé, Truffle Jus
recipes.visual_description: A single, meticulously composed portion rests upon an expansive white bone china plate. The centerpiece is a dark, perfectly seared rectangular block of compressed beef terrine, showcasing a rich, deep brown crust and a tender, dense interior. Adjacent to it, a golden-brown, equally precise rectangular block of crispy potato pavé rises, its layers subtly visible, offering a textural contrast. A glossy, dark truffle jus is artfully drizzled in a clean, elegant line or a delicate pool alongside the main components, catching the light. A few vibrant green micro-basil leaves are strategically placed on top of the beef terrine, providing a fresh pop of color. The plating emphasizes abundant negative space, highlighting the architectural precision and refined simplicity of each element. The scene is set on a pristine white Carrara marble surface, with dramatic, directional lighting creating subtle shadows that enhance depth and texture. A crisp white linen napkin, precisely folded into a triangle, sits nearby, completing the sophisticated, minimalist tableau.

ingredients.name: clarified butter or duck fat, for searing

instructions: Melt butter in a heavy-bottomed pan over medium heat. Sauté shallots until translucent, about 3 minutes. Add garlic; cook 1 minute more.
Add mincemeat. Break apart with a spoon. Brown evenly. Drain excess fat.
Pour in red wine. Reduce by half. Add beef stock, thyme, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper. Simmer 10 minutes until liquid is mostly absorbed.
Press the mixture into a parchment-lined terrine mold or small rectangular container (approx. 15cm x 10cm). Cover with another layer of parchment. Place a heavy weight on top.
Chill overnight in the refrigerator.
Slice peeled potatoes very thinly, ideally using a mandoline, into 1.5mm thick slices.
In a large bowl, combine cream, milk, garlic powder, onion powder, nutmeg, salt, and white pepper. Whisk well.
Add potato slices to the cream mixture. Toss gently to coat.
Layer potato slices tightly in a parchment-lined rectangular baking dish (approx. 15cm x 10cm). Press down firmly after each layer.
Bake at 160°C (325°F) for 1 hour 30 minutes, or until potatoes are tender.
Place parchment paper directly on top of the cooked potatoes. Apply a heavy weight. Chill overnight in the refrigerator.
Gently warm the beef demi-glace in a small saucepan over low heat.
Stir in truffle oil. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt. Keep warm.
Preheat oven to 180°C (350°F).
Unmold the compressed beef terrine. Cut into 4 equal, precise rectangular portions (approx. 7.5cm x 5cm each).
Unmold the potato pavé. Cut into 4 equal, precise rectangular portions (approx. 7.5cm x 5cm each).
Heat clarified butter in a non-stick pan over medium-high heat.
Carefully sear the beef terrine portions on all sides until a dark, crispy crust forms, about 2-3 minutes per side. Transfer to a baking sheet.
Sear the potato pavé portions in the same pan until golden and crispy on all sides, about 2-3 minutes per side. Transfer to the baking sheet.
Finish beef and potato in the preheated oven for 5-7 minutes, until heated through.
On each plate, carefully place one seared beef terrine portion. Place one seared potato pavé portion directly adjacent or slightly overlapping.
Spoon a clean, precise line or a small pool of truffle jus next to the beef and potato.
Garnish each plate with a few delicate micro-basil or micro-parsley leaves placed precisely on or near the beef.
Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Pollo alla Cacciatora con Patate
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Pollo alla Cacciatora is presented on a round, clean white porcelain dinner plate. A golden-brown, seared chicken thigh, its skin slightly crisped, rests at the center. Surrounding the chicken are generous chunks of tender, rustic potato wedges, vibrant red and green bell pepper pieces, and earthy quartered cremini mushrooms, all bathed in a rich, rustic red tomato sauce. The sauce, thickened naturally, coats the ingredients, showcasing flecks of dried oregano and chopped fresh rosemary. A scattering of bright green fresh parsley provides a final pop of color and freshness. The overall composition is balanced, showcasing the hearty textures and warm, inviting colors of a traditional Italian country dish. The plate sits on a simple wooden table, accompanied by standard silver flatware and a folded cotton napkin. Natural, even light illuminates the dish.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread (pane casereccio) to soak up the sauce.
Accompany with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and red wine vinegar.
A glass of red wine, such as Chianti or Sangiovese, is a traditional pairing.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and black pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs skin-side down until golden brown and crisp, about 6-8 minutes. Flip and sear other side for 3-4 minutes. Remove chicken and set aside.
Add diced onion to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in red and green bell peppers and quartered mushrooms. Cook for 5-7 minutes until slightly softened.
Pour in white wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Cook until wine is mostly reduced, about 2 minutes.
Add crushed tomatoes, chicken broth, dried oregano, fresh rosemary, and bay leaf. Bring to a simmer.
Return seared chicken thighs to the pot. Nestle them into the sauce. Ensure chicken is partially submerged.
Add potato wedges around the chicken.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 30-40 minutes, or until chicken is tender and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C/167°F) and potatoes are tender.
Uncover and simmer for an additional 5-10 minutes if sauce is too thin. Remove bay leaf.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley before serving.
notes: For best flavor, use good quality canned tomatoes.
Bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs provide more flavor and moisture.

recipes.recipe_name: Polpette di Patate e Carne con Funghi e Parmigiano
recipes.visual_description: Two to three golden-brown, oval-shaped polpette are artfully arranged on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, slightly off-center for balanced composition and moderate negative space. Each polpetta has a crisp, golden-brown exterior. A light sprinkle of vibrant green, finely chopped parsley garnishes the top, adding a fresh color contrast. The interior, if revealed, shows a creamy, light-brown potato and meat mixture flecked with darker, finely diced mushrooms and melted white mozzarella. The plate rests on a simple, light-toned wooden table. A neatly folded, off-white cotton napkin is placed beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the scene, evoking a warm, modern bistro atmosphere. A traditional silver fork rests alongside, hinting at an inviting dining experience with a softly blurred restaurant background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple marinara sauce on the side for dipping.
Accompanied by a small wedge of lemon.
instructions: Boil potatoes until very tender. Drain well. Mash thoroughly. Set aside to cool slightly.
Heat olive oil in a pan over medium heat. Sauté finely diced onion until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add mincemeat to the pan. Brown, breaking it up, until no pink remains. Drain any excess fat.
Add finely diced mushrooms. Cook until softened and moisture evaporates, about 5-7 minutes. Season with salt and pepper.
Transfer meat and mushroom mixture to a large bowl. Add mashed potatoes, grated Parmigiano Reggiano, shredded mozzarella, egg, 50g breadcrumbs, and chopped parsley.
Mix well until combined. Form into 12-16 oval or round polpette.
Place extra breadcrumbs in a shallow dish. Roll each polpetta in breadcrumbs to coat evenly.
Heat vegetable oil in a large skillet to 170°C (340°F). Fry polpette in batches for 3-4 minutes per side, until golden brown and cooked through.
Transfer to a wire rack lined with paper towels to drain excess oil.
Serve immediately.
notes: The polpette can be prepared ahead of time and refrigerated before frying.
Ensure the oil temperature is consistent for even browning and cooking.

recipes.recipe_name: Pollo alla Cacciatora con Tagliatelle
recipes.visual_description: A hearty single portion of Pollo alla Cacciatora is presented on a rustic, off-white ceramic plate. Two pieces of braised chicken, one thigh and one drumstick, are nestled among a generous mound of golden tagliatelle. The chicken is deeply browned, almost falling off the bone. The rich, chunky tomato-based sauce, flecked with tender red and green bell pepper strips, quartered mushrooms, and softened onions, generously coats the chicken and pasta. A scattering of fresh, bright green chopped parsley provides a pop of color. The plate sits on a well-used, warm-toned wooden dining table. A simple, silver fork and a casually placed linen napkin accompany the dish. The lighting is warm and cozy, evoking a lived-in family kitchen atmosphere. The scene is uncluttered, allowing the robust, comforting dish to be the focal point, reflecting authentic Italian home cooking.
instructions: Pat chicken pieces dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large, deep pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken pieces until golden brown on all sides. Do not overcrowd the pot. Work in batches if necessary. Remove chicken and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add chopped onion, red bell pepper strips, green bell pepper strips, and quartered mushrooms to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 8-10 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
If using, pour in red wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Cook until wine reduces by half.
Stir in crushed tomatoes, chicken broth, rosemary sprigs, thyme sprigs, and bay leaf. Bring to a simmer.
Return seared chicken pieces to the pot. Ensure chicken is mostly submerged in the sauce.
Reduce heat to low. Cover the pot. Simmer for 45-60 minutes, or until chicken is very tender and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C).
Remove rosemary, thyme, and bay leaf sprigs.
While chicken simmers, cook tagliatelle according to package instructions until al dente. Drain well.
Serve chicken and sauce over the cooked tagliatelle. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Cheesy Mincemeat Stuffed Mushrooms
recipes.visual_description: Four large, plump cremini mushrooms are elegantly plated as individual starters on a clean, round white porcelain plate. The mushroom caps are a rich, earthy brown, showcasing their natural form. Each mushroom is generously mounded with a savory mincemeat and potato stuffing, crowned with a golden, bubbly layer of melted cheddar cheese. Visible within the stuffing are flecks of green parsley and the darker texture of cooked mincemeat. A light sprinkle of vibrant fresh chopped parsley garnishes the top of the cheese, adding a pop of color. The plate is positioned on a simple wooden table surface, with a neatly folded cotton napkin and standard restaurant-style flatware placed beside it. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and inviting warmth. The background is minimal, suggesting a modern bistro setting, keeping the focus entirely on the appetizing starter.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.
Clean mushrooms. Gently remove stems. Finely chop mushroom stems.
Heat olive oil in a large pan over medium heat. Add diced onion. Sauté until translucent, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and chopped mushroom stems. Cook for 3 minutes more.
Add mincemeat to the pan. Brown thoroughly, breaking up clumps with a spoon. Cook until no pink remains. Drain any excess fat.
Stir in mashed potato, breadcrumbs, salt, and pepper. Mix well to combine all ingredients.
Remove pan from heat. Stir in half of the grated cheese and half of the chopped fresh parsley.
Spoon the mincemeat mixture generously into each mushroom cap, mounding it slightly.
Arrange stuffed mushrooms on a baking tray. Sprinkle remaining grated cheese over the top of each mushroom.
Bake for 20-25 minutes, or until mushrooms are tender and cheese is golden brown and bubbly. Ensure mincemeat internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Garnish with remaining fresh parsley. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Spanish Chicken and Potato Stew
recipes.visual_description: The dish features golden-browned chicken thigh chunks and irregular potato wedges in a rich, reddish-orange sauce. The potatoes are cracked with rough edges to thicken the stew naturally. Serve in a shallow terracotta cazuela on a rustic wooden table. The chicken is presented as whole bone-in pieces, never sliced. Sautéed onion and garlic bits are visible in the glossy sauce. A light sprinkle of chopped fresh parsley adds green contrast. The lighting is warm and domestic, suggesting a family kitchen. A crusty loaf of bread sits nearby on a linen cloth. The arrangement is casual and hearty, filling the bowl with a single, generous portion. Everything is captured in a clean, realistic photo.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty white bread for dipping.
Pair with a simple green salad.
Enjoy with a glass of light red wine.
instructions: Season chicken with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a deep pan over medium heat.
Brown chicken on all sides for 8 minutes.
Remove chicken and set aside.
Add diced onion to the pan.
Cook until translucent.
Add minced garlic and smoked paprika.
Stir for 1 minute.
Add potatoes cut into irregular chunks.
Return chicken to the pan.
Pour in chicken stock and add bay leaf.
Simmer for 25 minutes until potatoes are tender.
Check chicken reaches internal temperature of 75°C.
Remove bay leaf before serving.
Garnish with chopped parsley.
notes: Cracking the potatoes by snapping them off the knife releases starch to thicken the sauce naturally.
Use high-quality smoked pimentón for the most authentic flavor.

recipes.recipe_name: Cultured Egg & Radish Bites
recipes.visual_description: Eight to twelve elegant, bite-sized canapés are artfully arranged with consistent spacing on a light-colored, natural stone platter. White egg white halves are meticulously filled with a smooth, pale yellow yolk mixture. Each bite is topped with a single, paper-thin, round slice of vibrant red radish and a delicate sprig of fresh dill. These elegant components rest on small, irregular-shaped sourdough crisps. The composition showcases a clean palette of whites, pale yellows, and striking reds and greens, emphasizing natural ingredient beauty. Textures range from creamy yolk to firm egg white, crisp radish, and crunchy sourdough. The platter sits on a light, reclaimed wood table surface. Soft, diffused natural light illuminates the scene, creating gentle shadows. A folded, undyed linen napkin in a natural beige tone subtly complements the setting. The background is clean and minimalist, with a hint of lush green foliage suggesting a connection to nature.
instructions: Hard-boil eggs. Cool completely in ice water. Peel eggs carefully.
Slice each egg in half lengthwise. Gently scoop out yolks into a small bowl. Place egg whites on a clean surface.
Mash yolks thoroughly with a fork. Add mayonnaise, Dijon mustard, fermented chili paste, salt, and pepper. Mix until smooth and creamy.
Toast sourdough slices until crisp. Break into irregular, bite-sized crisps. Drizzle lightly with olive oil.
Using a small spoon or piping bag, fill each egg white half with the yolk mixture.
Wash radishes. Slice radishes into paper-thin rounds using a mandoline or sharp knife. If radish greens are young and tender, reserve a few small leaves for garnish.
Arrange filled egg halves on the sourdough crisps.
Garnish each canapé with a single radish slice and a small sprig of fresh dill or finely chopped chives. Add reserved radish greens if using.
Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Tomato & Chicken Rice Bowl
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of the Fermented Tomato & Chicken Rice Bowl is presented in a deep, matte cream-colored ceramic bowl. A mound of fluffy Basmati rice forms the base. Tender, golden-brown chicken chunks are nestled on one side, glistening with a savory pan sauce. Adjacent, a vibrant cluster of halved, quick-brined cherry tomatoes adds a pop of deep red and tangy texture. Thinly sliced quick-pickled red onions are scattered over, their translucent purple-pink hues contrasting beautifully. A sprinkle of fresh green parsley adds a final touch. The presentation is clean, minimalistic, and natural, with ample negative space. The bowl rests on a light, reclaimed wooden surface, accompanied by simple wooden chopsticks and an undyed linen napkin, evoking an eco-conscious, rustic elegance. Soft, natural light highlights the ingredients' colors and textures.
instructions: Prepare Quick-Brined Tomatoes: Wash 500g cherry tomatoes. Halve them. In a bowl, combine tomatoes with 5g salt, 5g sugar, and 30ml apple cider vinegar. Stir. Let sit at room temperature while preparing other ingredients.

Prepare Quick Pickled Red Onions: Thinly slice 1 medium red onion. In a small saucepan, combine 120ml apple cider vinegar, 60ml water, 15g sugar, and 5g salt. Bring to a simmer until sugar and salt dissolve. Pour hot liquid over sliced red onion in a heatproof bowl. Let cool.

Cook Rice: Rinse 300g Basmati rice until water runs clear. In a saucepan, combine rice with 600ml water. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 12-15 minutes until water is absorbed. Remove from heat. Let stand covered for 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork.

Cook Chicken: Dice 1 large brown onion. Mince 3 garlic cloves. Grate 2cm ginger. Cut 600g chicken thighs into 3-4 cm chunks. Season chicken with salt and pepper. Heat 15ml olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Sear chicken chunks until golden brown on all sides. Remove chicken from pan.
Add remaining 15ml olive oil to the pan. Add diced brown onion. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic and grated ginger. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Return chicken to the pan. Pour in 500ml chicken stock. Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low. Cover and cook for 15-20 minutes, or until chicken is cooked through (internal temperature 75°C).

Assemble Bowls: Divide cooked rice among 4 deep bowls. Spoon chicken and its sauce over the rice. Drain quick-brined tomatoes and spoon a generous amount next to the chicken. Drain quick-pickled red onions and scatter over the dish. Garnish with chopped fresh parsley or coriander.
notes: For enhanced flavor and zero-waste, use chicken bones and vegetable scraps to make homemade chicken stock.
Adjust the amount of sugar and vinegar in the quick-pickled red onions to your preferred balance of sweetness and sourness.

recipes.recipe_name: French Braised Beef with Roasted Potatoes and Pearl Onions
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of French Braised Beef is presented on a clean, wide white porcelain dinner plate. Generous, irregular chunks of dark, fork-tender braised beef are the centerpiece, glistening with a rich, deep brown red wine reduction sauce spooned over them and pooling at the base. Surrounding the beef are golden-brown roasted potato wedges, their skins slightly crisp, and glistening amber caramelized pearl onions. A scattering of bright green chopped fresh parsley provides a vibrant contrast. The composition is balanced and elegant, with moderate negative space. The plate rests on a simple wooden table surface in a modern bistro setting. A crisp white cotton napkin is folded beside the plate, and a crusty slice of baguette is placed near the edge, ready for dipping. Natural, even lighting highlights the textures and colors of the dish, with a softly blurred, casual restaurant background.
instructions: Pat beef chuck roast dry. Cut into 5-6 cm chunks. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven or oven-safe pot over medium-high heat. Sear beef chunks in batches until deeply browned on all sides. Remove beef and set aside.
Dice large yellow onion. Add to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes. Mince garlic cloves. Add to pot. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Sprinkle flour over onions and garlic. Stir for 1 minute. Deglaze with red wine, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Cook until wine is mostly evaporated.
Return beef to the pot. Add beef broth, thyme sprigs, and bay leaf. Bring to a simmer. Cover and transfer to a preheated oven at 160°C.
Braise for 2.5 to 3 hours, or until beef is fork-tender.

While beef braises, preheat oven to 200°C. Halve or quarter small new potatoes. Toss with a drizzle of olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking sheet. Roast for 30-40 minutes until golden brown and tender.
Peel pearl onions. Heat butter in a small skillet over medium heat. Add pearl onions. Cook, stirring occasionally, until caramelized and tender, about 15-20 minutes.
Once beef is tender, remove from oven. Remove beef chunks and set aside. Strain the braising liquid through a fine-mesh sieve into a saucepan. Discard solids and herbs.
Bring braising liquid to a simmer over medium-high heat. Reduce until slightly thickened and glossy, about 10-15 minutes. Adjust seasoning if needed.
Chop fresh parsley. Arrange beef chunks, roasted potatoes, and caramelized pearl onions on individual plates. Spoon reduced sauce generously over the beef. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Baked Rigatoni with Smoked Provolone, Ricotta, and Artichoke
recipes.visual_description: A single generous portion of baked rigatoni is presented in a clean, off-white porcelain pasta bowl, set on a simple light wooden table. The rigatoni is coated in a rich, creamy sauce, with visible pieces of chopped artichoke hearts (1 cm pieces) and melted cheeses. The top surface features a beautiful golden-brown, bubbly crust from the baked smoked provolone and crispy panko breadcrumbs. The interior of the dish shows tender rigatoni tubes, some holding pockets of the creamy ricotta-based sauce. Specks of vibrant green fresh parsley are sprinkled over the top, adding a pop of color. The overall color palette is warm, with creamy whites and light browns contrasting with the green of the artichoke and parsley. The dish has a comforting, hearty texture. A silver fork and knife are placed neatly to the right of the bowl on a folded cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and colors without harsh shadows. The background is minimal, suggesting a casual bistro atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread.
Pair with a simple green salad.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C (375°F).
Cook rigatoni according to package directions until al dente. Drain and set aside.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet or Dutch oven over medium heat.
Add diced onion. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in chopped artichoke hearts. Cook for 2 minutes.
Deglaze with strong brewed coffee. Simmer until liquid is almost absorbed.
In a separate saucepan, melt butter over medium heat.
Whisk in flour to form a roux. Cook for 1 minute.
Gradually whisk in heavy cream and vegetable broth. Cook, stirring, until sauce thickens.
Remove sauce from heat. Stir in ricotta cheese and 100 g of shredded smoked provolone until melted and smooth.
Stir in mayonnaise, salt, pepper, and nutmeg. Taste and adjust seasoning.
Combine cooked rigatoni with the cheese sauce in the skillet or a large baking dish. Mix well to coat all pasta.
Top with remaining 50 g shredded smoked provolone and panko breadcrumbs.
Bake for 20-25 minutes, or until bubbling and golden brown on top.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Yogurt-Marinated Chicken with Fermented Tomato Relish and Creamy Macaroni Salad
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a natural cream-colored handcrafted ceramic plate, showcasing a single, generously portioned serving. A golden-brown seared chicken breast, whole, rests on one side of the plate. Its surface reveals a subtle char from the pan-searing. Adjacent to the chicken is a vibrant, chunky mound of fermented tomato relish, displaying a rich medley of red tomato pieces, pale diced onion, and specks of green dill. The relish has a rustic, slightly irregular texture. On the other side of the plate, a creamy macaroni salad is neatly scooped, revealing tender macaroni, bright orange shredded carrot, crisp green cucumber pieces, and earthy mushroom bits. A sprinkle of golden toasted breadcrumbs adds texture to the macaroni, and a fresh dill sprig garnishes the salad, providing a touch of green. The overall composition is clean and minimalist, with ample white space on the plate. The setting features a light, textured reclaimed wood table surface, with an undyed linen napkin draped casually. Soft, natural light illuminates the scene, highlighting the fresh, natural colors and textures of the ingredients.
instructions: Combine yogurt, minced garlic, lemon zest and juice, orange zest, olive oil, salt, and black pepper in a bowl. Add chicken breasts. Coat well. Marinate in refrigerator for at least 2 hours, or overnight.

In a clean jar or bowl, combine diced tomatoes, finely diced red onion, minced garlic, sugar, salt, black pepper, and lemon juice. Stir well. Cover loosely. Let sit at room temperature for 12-24 hours to lightly ferment. Refrigerate after fermentation. Stir in chopped dill before serving.
Bring a pot of salted water to a boil. Add macaroni. Cook according to package directions until al dente. Drain well. Rinse with cold water to stop cooking. Drain again thoroughly.

In a large bowl, combine cooked macaroni, mayonnaise, yogurt, milk, diced cucumber, shredded carrot, finely diced mushrooms, chopped hard-boiled egg (if using), and grated cheese. Add chopped dill, salt, and black pepper. Mix gently until all ingredients are coated. Refrigerate until ready to serve.

Heat a large pan over medium-high heat. Remove chicken from marinade, shaking off excess. Sear chicken breasts for 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C). Rest chicken for 5 minutes before serving.

Plate a single chicken breast. Spoon a generous portion of creamy macaroni salad next to it. Add a spoonful of fermented tomato relish. Garnish the macaroni salad with toasted breadcrumbs and a fresh dill sprig.
notes: To make this recipe even more zero-waste, save chicken bones for homemade stock.
Leftover citrus peels can be dried and used for infused water or tea.
Vegetable scraps from carrots and onions can be saved for making vegetable broth.
Stale bread can be used to make the toasted breadcrumbs.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Keema Pulao
recipes.visual_description: A single generous serving of Chicken Keema Pulao is presented on a rustic, round ceramic plate with a subtle, earthy glaze. The basmati rice is fluffy, absorbing a rich, golden-brown hue from the spices, visibly mixed with small, tender chunks of savory chicken mincemeat. Finely diced, caramelized onions are interspersed throughout. Vibrant green flecks of chopped fresh coriander and mint leaves are scattered over the top, providing a fresh contrast. The dish is casually mounded, allowing natural negative space. The chicken mincemeat is thoroughly cooked. The overall appearance is hearty and comforting. The plate rests on a well-used wooden dining table, illuminated by warm kitchen lighting. A simple metal spoon is beside the plate. A small, plain ceramic bowl of cooling Raita is to the side.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of Raita (yogurt dip).
Accompanied by pickled onions or a simple green salad.
instructions: Wash basmati rice thoroughly. Soak in water for 30 minutes. Drain well.
Heat ghee in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat. Add cinnamon stick, cardamom pods, cloves, and bay leaf. Sauté 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add diced onions. Sauté until golden brown, about 8-10 minutes.
Add ginger-garlic paste and slit green chilies. Sauté 1 minute until aromatic.
Add chicken mincemeat. Cook, breaking up clumps with a spoon, until browned and cooked through. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F).
Add chopped tomatoes, turmeric powder, red chili powder, and coriander powder. Cook, stirring occasionally, until tomatoes soften and oil separates from the mixture, about 5-7 minutes.
Add drained basmati rice to the pot. Gently mix with the chicken and spices for 1 minute.
Pour in water and add salt. Bring the mixture to a rolling boil.
Reduce heat to low. Cover the pot tightly with a lid. Cook for 15-20 minutes, until all water is absorbed and rice is tender.
Remove pot from heat. Let it stand, covered, for 10 minutes (dum cooking).
Open lid. Gently fluff the rice with a fork. Mix in garam masala, chopped fresh coriander, and chopped fresh mint leaves.
Serve hot.
notes: Ensure chicken mincemeat reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
Adjust green chilies to your preferred spice level.

recipes.recipe_name: Cabbage and Chicken Chopped Salad
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant and hearty Cabbage and Chicken Chopped Salad is presented in an everyday ceramic bowl, typical of a family kitchen. The salad is mounded generously, showcasing a rich array of colors and textures. Finely shredded green cabbage forms the base, interspersed with visible diced chicken chunks, bright red tomato pieces, crisp green cucumber, yellow corn kernels, and vibrant green peas. Diced bell pepper, thinly sliced mushrooms, and black olives add further visual interest. Shredded cheddar cheese and a creamy, light-colored dressing are visibly integrated, coating the ingredients. The presentation is natural and unpretentious. The bowl sits on a well-used wooden dining table. Lighting is warm and cozy, suggestive of a relaxed family meal. A simple paper towel is casually placed nearby. The scene conveys homely comfort.
instructions: Dice chicken breasts into 2 cm cubes. Cook chicken in a pan with a little oil until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Set aside to cool.
Finely shred cabbage. Dice tomatoes, cucumber, bell pepper, and onion into 1 cm pieces. Thinly slice mushrooms.
Rinse and drain preserved black beans. Drain corn. Thaw green peas. Slice black olives.
Shred cheddar cheese.
For the dressing, mince garlic. In a medium bowl, whisk together sour cream, minced garlic, olive oil, white vinegar, salt, pepper, and sugar until smooth.

In a large mixing bowl, combine shredded cabbage, cooled diced chicken, diced tomatoes, diced cucumber, corn, green peas, diced bell pepper, sliced mushrooms, sliced olives, and rinsed black beans. Add shredded cheese.
Pour the prepared dressing over the salad ingredients. Gently toss until all components are evenly coated.
Serve immediately in individual portions.

recipes.recipe_name: Classic Chicken Parmesan
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Classic Chicken Parmesan rests on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, centered on a rustic wooden table. The golden-brown, pan-fried chicken cutlet, approximately 1 cm thick, is generously covered with a vibrant red marinara sauce. Melted, bubbly fresh mozzarella and grated Parmesan cheese form a golden, gooey crust over the chicken. Scattered fresh green basil leaves provide a vivid color contrast. The chicken is presented as a whole piece, maintaining its crispy texture. The plate has moderate negative space, allowing the dish to stand out. A simple white linen napkin and a silver fork and knife are placed beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and rich colors, with a subtly blurred background suggesting a casual bistro setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve alongside a portion of spaghetti or penne pasta tossed with extra marinara sauce.
Offer a simple green salad with a light vinaigrette.
Provide crusty Italian bread for dipping in the sauce.

ingredients.name: Fresh mozzarella cheese, sliced or shredded

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Lightly grease a baking dish.
Place each chicken breast between two sheets of plastic wrap. Pound with a meat mallet to a uniform thickness of 1 cm (approx. 180g cutlets). Season both sides with salt and pepper.
Prepare a breading station: Place flour in a shallow dish. Whisk eggs in a second shallow dish. Place breadcrumbs in a third shallow dish.
Dredge each chicken cutlet in flour, shaking off excess. Dip in egg wash, allowing excess to drip off. Coat thoroughly with breadcrumbs, pressing gently to adhere.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Fry chicken cutlets for 3-4 minutes per side, until golden brown and crispy. Do not overcrowd the pan; cook in batches if necessary.
Transfer fried chicken cutlets to the prepared baking dish.
Sauté minced garlic in the same skillet for 30 seconds until fragrant. Pour in marinara sauce. Bring to a gentle simmer. Season with salt and pepper.
Spoon a generous amount of marinara sauce over each chicken cutlet. Top with fresh mozzarella slices/shreds and grated Parmesan cheese.
Bake for 15-20 minutes, or until cheese is melted and bubbly, and chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C. The breading should be golden brown.
Remove from oven. Garnish with fresh basil leaves. Serve immediately.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
Pounding the chicken to an even thickness ensures uniform cooking and tenderness.

recipes.recipe_name: Cabbage, Chicken, and Creamy Vegetable Salad
recipes.visual_description: A generous, homely portion of Cabbage, Chicken, and Creamy Vegetable Salad is presented on a simple, round, off-white ceramic plate. Shredded green cabbage forms a natural base, generously mixed with vibrant diced red tomatoes, crisp diced cucumber, bright yellow corn kernels, dark black beans, and diced red bell pepper. Tender diced chicken chunks are interspersed throughout. Thawed green peas and sautéed brown mushroom slices add textural variety. Sliced black olives are visible. A creamy, white dressing lightly coats all ingredients, with a sprinkle of shredded orange Cheddar cheese on top. The arrangement is casual and unpretentious, with components naturally touching and overlapping. The plate sits on a well-used, warm-toned wooden kitchen table. A simple metal fork and a folded cloth napkin are placed beside the plate. Warm, soft lighting from an overhead kitchen fixture illuminates the scene, creating a cozy, lived-in family dining atmosphere.
instructions: Pat chicken breast dry. Season with salt and pepper. Heat 15 ml olive oil in a pan over medium-high heat. Sear chicken 5-7 minutes per side until cooked through and internal temperature reaches 75°C. Let rest 5 minutes. Dice into 2 cm chunks.
Shred cabbage thinly. Dice tomatoes, cucumber, and red bell pepper into 1 cm cubes.
Rinse black beans under cold water. Drain corn kernels. Thaw green peas.
Slice mushrooms. Heat remaining 15 ml olive oil in the same pan. Sauté sliced mushrooms 5-7 minutes until browned and tender. Let cool.
Slice black olives into rounds.
For the dressing: Finely dice half red onion. Mince garlic clove. In a bowl, whisk together sour cream, diced red onion, minced garlic, white vinegar, salt, and pepper until smooth.
In a large mixing bowl, combine shredded cabbage, diced tomatoes, diced cucumber, black beans, corn, red bell pepper, green peas, sautéed mushrooms, and sliced olives.
Add diced chicken chunks to the vegetable mixture. Pour the sour cream dressing over the salad. Toss gently to coat all ingredients evenly.
Shred Cheddar cheese. Serve salad immediately, topped with shredded cheese.

recipes.recipe_name: Cajun Beer-Braised Chicken and Spicy Rice
recipes.visual_description: A generous portion of vibrant Cajun Beer-Braised Chicken and Spicy Rice is plated on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. Two seasoned, golden-brown chicken thighs are nestled atop the reddish-brown, moist rice. The rice is studded with finely diced red tomato, green bell pepper, and onion. Freshly chopped green parsley sprinkles over the dish, with a light melt of shredded sharp cheddar cheese on the chicken. The plating is natural and mounded, professional yet approachable. The dish rests on a light wooden table surface, implying a modern bistro setting. A neatly folded off-white cotton napkin is placed to the left. Natural, even lighting illuminates the food, highlighting textures and colors. The background is softly blurred, showing a casual restaurant ambiance.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with extra hot sauce on the side.
Serve with cornbread or French bread.
Pair with a cold lager beer.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with Cajun seasoning, salt, and pepper.
Heat 30ml vegetable oil in a large Dutch oven or heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken skin-side down until deep golden brown and crispy. Flip and sear other side. Remove chicken from pot.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion, bell pepper, and celery to the pot. Cook until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in 300g uncooked rice. Cook 2 minutes, stirring to coat.
Pour in 330ml beer and scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Bring to a simmer.
Stir in 400g diced tomatoes with their juice, 500ml chicken broth, and 15ml hot sauce. Bring to a boil.
Return chicken to the pot, skin-side up, nestling it into the rice mixture. Ensure liquid mostly covers rice.
Reduce heat to low. Cover pot tightly. Simmer 20-25 minutes, or until rice is tender and chicken reaches 75°C (167°F).
Remove from heat. Let stand covered 5 minutes.
Fluff rice gently with a fork. Serve immediately.
notes: Adjust hot sauce quantity to desired spice level.
Ensure rice is fully cooked but not mushy.

recipes.recipe_name: Clarified Chicken Consommé with Poached Chicken Roulade and Garden Brunoise
recipes.visual_description: A single, meticulously composed portion rests in a wide, shallow, pristine white bone china bowl. The liquid is a crystal-clear, shimmering golden consommé, profoundly clear. Elegantly centered are two to three precisely cut, circular medallions of poached chicken roulade, their pure white flesh subtly contrasted by visible green herbs. Surrounding the roulade, a scattering of vibrant, jewel-like brunoise-cut vegetables—bright orange carrot, pale green celery, translucent white leek—adds precise color and texture. A delicate swirl of verdant chive oil floats on the consommé's surface. A small sprig of micro chervil crowns the chicken. The composition rests on a premium grey-veined marble surface, flanked by a pristine white linen napkin folded into a sharp triangle and a modern, minimalist spoon. Dramatic, focused lighting with soft shadows emphasizes exquisite simplicity and abundant negative space.
instructions: Prepare Chicken Stock: Combine chicken bones, onion, carrots, celery, leek, thyme, bay leaves, and peppercorns in a large stockpot. Add cold water. Bring slowly to a simmer, skimming impurities. Reduce heat to low. Simmer gently for 4-6 hours. Strain stock through a fine-mesh sieve lined with cheesecloth. Cool completely. Degrease thoroughly.

Prepare Chicken Roulade: Pound chicken breasts to an even 0.5 cm thickness. Season lightly with salt and pepper. Sprinkle half the tarragon and chervil evenly over each breast. Roll each breast tightly into a cylinder. Wrap tightly in plastic wrap or vacuum seal in sous-vide bags. Cook in a water bath at 65°C (149°F) for 1 hour. Immediately transfer to an ice bath to chill. Once chilled, unwrap and slice into 1.5 cm thick medallions. Store refrigerated.

Prepare Consommé Clarification Raft: In a large bowl, combine chicken mince, diced onion, diced carrot, diced celery, and egg whites. Mix thoroughly. Gradually whisk in 500 ml of cold, degreased chicken stock until well combined.

Clarify Consommé: Add the clarification raft mixture to the remaining cold chicken stock in a large pot. Place over medium-low heat. Stir gently but constantly until raft begins to form and float to the surface. Stop stirring. Create a small "chimney" in the center of the raft. Maintain a very gentle simmer for 45-60 minutes, allowing clear liquid to bubble through the chimney. Do not boil.
Strain Consommé: Carefully ladle the clear consommé through a fine-mesh sieve lined with a clean, damp cheesecloth or coffee filter. Do not press the raft. Season with salt to taste. Keep warm.
Prepare Garden Brunoise: Blanch diced carrot, celery, and leek separately in salted boiling water for 30 seconds. Immediately transfer to an ice bath. Drain well.

Prepare Chive Oil: Blanch chives in boiling water for 10 seconds. Immediately transfer to an ice bath. Drain and squeeze dry. Blend chives with olive oil and a pinch of salt until smooth. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve lined with cheesecloth.

Assemble and Serve: Gently warm sliced chicken roulade medallions in a little consommé or steam lightly. Place 2-3 roulade medallions in the center of each deep, warm serving bowl. Scatter a small amount of blanched garden brunoise around the roulade. Carefully ladle the hot, clear consommé into the bowl. Drizzle a few drops of chive oil over the surface. Garnish with micro chervil or micro tarragon. Serve immediately. Ensure chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F) during warming.
notes: Ensure the chicken stock is thoroughly degreased for optimal consommé clarity.
Do not let the consommé boil during clarification, as it will break the raft and cloud the liquid.
Achieving proper sous-vide chicken internal temperature is crucial for food safety and tenderness.
Blanching the brunoise briefly keeps them vibrant and tender-crisp.

recipes.recipe_name: Seared Chicken Roulade, Potato Pavé, Broccoli Emulsion, Onion Jus, Parmesan Crisp
recipes.visual_description: A single, exquisitely plated starter portion sits centered on a large, round bone china plate, allowing for abundant negative space. A thick, golden-brown seared chicken roulade medallion, perfectly cooked to a tender, moist interior, is the focal point. Adjacent to it rests a precise, rectangular potato pavé, its layers visible, with a crisp, golden exterior. A small, vibrant green pool or artful swipe of smooth broccoli emulsion adds a pop of color and creamy texture. Beneath or alongside these elements, a clear, deep amber pool of glossy onion jus subtly enhances the composition. A delicate, irregularly shaped Parmesan crisp, thin and golden, leans elegantly against the chicken, providing a contrasting textural element. The overall presentation is minimalist and architectural, with each component intentionally placed to create a harmonious, flowing composition. The plate rests on a premium white Carrara marble surface. Polished silver fine-dining cutlery is neatly arranged to the right. A pristine white linen napkin, folded into a precise triangle, complements the setting. Dramatic, soft overhead lighting casts subtle shadows, highlighting the dish's textures and colors. The background is ultra-minimalist, drawing all focus to the meticulously prepared food.

ingredients.name: Chicken breasts, skin on, bone out
Floury potatoes (e.g., Russet or Maris Piper)

instructions: Prepare Chicken Roulade: Trim chicken breasts. Butterfly open. Pound flat between parchment paper to uniform thickness. Season generously with salt and pepper.

Make chicken mousse: Combine chicken thigh meat, 50ml double cream, 2g fresh thyme, 2g fresh chives, 2g salt, and 0.5g white pepper in a food processor. Blend until very smooth. Pass through a fine-mesh sieve for ultra-smoothness.
Spread mousse evenly over each butterflied chicken breast. Roll tightly into a cylinder. Secure tightly with cling film, forming a compact roulade. Alternatively, use butcher's twine.
Sous-vide chicken roulades at 63°C for 1.5 hours. Alternatively, gently poach in simmering water until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Rapidly chill in an ice bath.
Once cold, remove cling film or twine. Just before serving, sear roulades in hot olive oil until golden brown and crispy on all sides. Baste with a knob of butter. Rest 5 minutes.
Prepare Potato Pavé: Peel potatoes. Slice very thinly using a mandoline (1-2mm thickness).
Combine 100ml double cream, 50ml whole milk, crushed garlic, 1 sprig fresh thyme, 5g salt, and 0.5g white pepper in a small saucepan. Heat gently; do not boil.
Lightly grease and line a small terrine mould or baking dish (approx. 10x15cm) with parchment paper.

Arrange potato slices in layers in the mould, overlapping slightly. Brush each layer with melted butter and some cream mixture. Press firmly between layers to remove air pockets. Repeat until all potatoes are used.
Bake at 160°C for 60-75 minutes, or until potatoes are tender when pierced. Place a heavy weight on top of the cooked pavé and chill overnight (or at least 4 hours) to compress.
Once chilled and compressed, remove from mould. Cut into precise rectangular portions (approx. 3x5cm). Just before serving, sear or bake pavé portions until golden and crispy on all sides.
Prepare Broccoli Emulsion: Blanch broccoli florets in generously salted boiling water for 2-3 minutes. Immediately transfer to an ice bath to stop cooking and preserve color. Drain very well.

Blend blanched broccoli with 50ml vegetable stock, 30ml extra virgin olive oil, 5g salt, and a pinch of white pepper until extremely smooth. For an airy emulsion, add 2g soy lecithin and use an immersion blender right before serving. Pass through a fine-mesh sieve for ultimate smoothness. Reheat gently before plating.
Prepare Onion Jus: Sauté thinly sliced yellow onions in a little olive oil over low heat for 20-30 minutes until deeply caramelized and sweet. Do not burn.
Deglaze pan with 50ml dry white wine. Scrape up any fond. Reduce wine by half.
Add 500ml chicken stock, 15ml sherry vinegar, 2g black peppercorns, 1 sprig fresh thyme, and 1 bay leaf. Simmer gently for 30-45 minutes, reducing by half. Skim any impurities.

Strain jus through a fine-mesh sieve, pressing solids to extract maximum flavor. Reduce further if needed for desired glossy, coating consistency. Just before serving, whisk in 5g cold unsalted butter for richness and shine. Season to taste.
Prepare Parmesan Crisp: Preheat oven to 180°C. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Spread grated Parmigiano-Reggiano thinly in desired irregular, organic shapes on the parchment paper. Leave space between crisps.
Bake for 5-8 minutes, or until golden brown and crisp. Watch carefully to prevent burning. Cool on a wire rack; crisps will harden as they cool.
Assembly: Slice chilled, seared chicken roulade into 2cm thick medallions. Reheat gently if needed. Reheat potato pavé portions.
On each large, round bone china plate, spoon a small, artful pool or swipe of onion jus.
Carefully place one seared chicken medallion and one potato pavé portion beside the jus, creating an elegant composition.
Add a precise dot or small, artful streak of vibrant green broccoli emulsion. Maintain abundant negative space on the plate.
Gently lean one irregular parmesan crisp against the chicken or pavé for height and texture.
Garnish minimally with a few microgreens for a final touch of freshness and color. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Cheesy Baked Chicken with Roasted Tomatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Cheesy Baked Chicken with Roasted Tomatoes rests on a simple, off-white ceramic plate. A tender, golden-brown boneless chicken thigh is positioned centrally, generously covered with melted, bubbly mozzarella and Parmesan cheese that shows light golden-brown spots. Surrounding the chicken are halved, roasted cherry tomatoes, some burst open, revealing their juicy interior. Soft, golden-brown garlic slices are nestled among the tomatoes. The arrangement is casual and natural, typical of home cooking, with components slightly overlapping. Fresh green basil leaves are scattered over the dish, providing a pop of color. The plate is set on a well-used wooden dining table, revealing its natural grain and subtle imperfections. A simple, folded cloth napkin and standard flatware (fork and knife) are casually placed beside the plate. Warm, inviting light from a kitchen fixture illuminates the scene, creating a cozy, lived-in atmosphere. The background is minimal, suggesting a relaxed family dining area.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread to soak up the flavorful pan juices.
Accompany with a simple green salad dressed with vinaigrette.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Ensure chicken is at room temperature.
Pat chicken thighs dry with paper towels. Season chicken with salt and pepper.
Halve cherry tomatoes. Thinly slice garlic cloves.
In a large baking dish, combine chicken, halved cherry tomatoes, sliced garlic, olive oil, and dried oregano. Toss to coat all ingredients evenly.
Arrange chicken in a single layer in the dish. Distribute tomatoes and garlic around chicken.
Bake for 25 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 70°C.
Remove dish from oven. Sprinkle shredded mozzarella and grated Parmesan over chicken and vegetables.
Return to oven. Bake for another 10-15 minutes, or until cheese is melted, bubbly, and lightly golden. Chicken internal temperature should reach 75°C.
Remove from oven. Let rest for 5 minutes.
Garnish with fresh basil leaves before serving.
notes: This dish is perfect for a weeknight family meal.
Adjust garlic quantity to personal preference.
For extra flavor, use bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs and increase baking time slightly.

recipes.recipe_name: Beef Tenderloin Tartare, Black Garlic Emulsion, Sourdough Crisp
recipes.visual_description: A pristine white Carrara marble slab serves as the minimalist canvas. Four distinct, artfully composed portions of Beef Tenderloin Tartare are arranged with precision. Each portion features a perfectly formed, glistening quenelle of ruby-red, finely diced beef, reflecting subtle highlights. Beside each quenelle, an irregular, golden-brown shard of delicate sourdough crisp stands upright, offering textural contrast. Dots of rich, obsidian-black black garlic emulsion are strategically placed around the tartare, creating a sophisticated visual flow. A few vibrant green chive batons are meticulously placed atop each tartare quenelle, providing a fresh pop of color. Abundant negative space surrounds each composition, emphasizing the architectural elegance and restraint. Dramatic, focused lighting casts subtle shadows, enhancing the dish's sculptural quality. The presentation is refined, showcasing premium ingredients with exceptional clarity and purpose.
instructions: Preheat oven to 160°C.
Brush sourdough slices with melted butter. Bake until golden and very crisp. Break into irregular shards. Set aside.
Blend black garlic with mayonnaise until completely smooth. Season with salt. Transfer to a piping bag or small bowl. Refrigerate.
Finely dice beef tenderloin into small, uniform cubes.
In a mixing bowl, combine diced beef with finely minced shallot, chopped capers, chopped cornichons, Dijon mustard, egg yolk, and olive oil. Gently mix.
Season beef mixture generously with sea salt and black pepper. Taste and adjust seasoning.
On a premium white sharing platter, arrange small quenelles of beef tartare. Use two spoons to form quenelles.
Artfully place sourdough crisp shards beside each tartare quenelle.
Pipe or spoon small dots of black garlic emulsion around the tartare.
Garnish each tartare quenelle with a few chive batons.
Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Spanish Chicken with Paprika Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Roasted Spanish Chicken with Paprika Potatoes is presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate. A golden-brown, crispy-skinned chicken thigh is centered, showcasing its succulent appearance. Surrounding the chicken are artfully arranged, rustic paprika-dusted potato wedges, their edges lightly caramelized. Vibrant halved cherry tomatoes burst with color, interspersed with tender, translucent wedges of roasted red onion and a few roasted, smashed garlic cloves. A sprinkle of fresh, bright green chopped parsley provides a contrasting garnish. The dish is arranged with moderate negative space, creating a balanced and appealing composition. The setting features a simple wooden table surface, with a cotton napkin placed neatly beside the plate and traditional European flatware. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's rich colors and textures, creating an inviting, casual bistro atmosphere.

ingredients.name: Potatoes, small (e.g., desiree or new potatoes)

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (fan-forced 180°C).
Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and black pepper.
Wash potatoes. Cut into 2cm thick wedges.
Peel red onion. Cut into 2cm thick wedges.
Smash garlic cloves lightly, leave skins on.
In a large bowl, combine potato wedges, onion wedges, and smashed garlic. Drizzle with 2 tablespoons olive oil and smoked paprika. Toss to coat evenly.
Arrange chicken thighs, potatoes, onion, and garlic in a single layer on a large baking tray. Do not overcrowd.
Roast for 25 minutes. Carefully flip chicken and potatoes.
Pour chicken broth over vegetables. Continue roasting for another 15 minutes.
Add cherry tomatoes to the tray. Continue roasting for 10-15 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) and potatoes are tender and golden.
Remove from oven. Let rest 5 minutes.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Strawberry Granita with Citrus Tuile
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of light pink Fermented Strawberry Granita is presented in a handcrafted, unglazed ceramic bowl, in a natural cream or beige tone. The granita is scraped into delicate, icy flakes, creating a soft, ethereal mound. Alongside, a single, irregular, thin citrus tuile, golden-brown and slightly curved, leans elegantly against the granita or rests on the bowl's rim. The plating emphasizes clean lines and ample white space around the food, highlighting the pure beauty of the ingredients. A tiny, vibrant green mint leaf or a delicate edible flower petal is placed minimally on the granita for a subtle color contrast. The setting is an eco-conscious light bamboo or reclaimed wood table surface, providing a natural texture. An undyed linen napkin in a natural beige tone is subtly draped. Soft, natural lighting illuminates the dish, creating gentle shadows. The background is clean and uncluttered, with a hint of natural elements like a blurred plant, maintaining a minimalist aesthetic.
instructions: Combine quartered strawberries with 50g granulated sugar in a clean glass jar. Stir gently. Cover loosely with a cloth or lid, allowing air circulation. Let sit at room temperature (20-24°C) for 24-48 hours. Stir once or twice. This allows natural yeasts to begin a light fermentation, developing complex flavors.
After fermentation, transfer strawberries and their syrup to a blender. Add 200ml water, 30g granulated sugar, and strawberry vodka. Blend until smooth. Taste and adjust sweetness if desired.

Pour the mixture into a shallow metal pan or freezer-safe dish. Freeze for 1 hour. Scrape the icy edges towards the center with a fork. Repeat this scraping process every 30-45 minutes until the mixture forms light, icy flakes. This takes approximately 3-4 hours.
For the citrus tuiles, whisk together flour, powdered sugar, melted butter, and egg white in a small bowl until smooth. Stir in the finely grated citrus zest.
Preheat oven to 160°C. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Drop small spoonfuls of batter onto the parchment paper. Use the back of the spoon to spread thinly into irregular, organic shapes. Leave space between each.

Bake for 5-7 minutes, or until edges are golden brown and crisp. Watch carefully to prevent burning. Remove from oven. Immediately lift tuiles with a spatula and place over a rolling pin or curved surface to create a subtle curve as they cool. Let cool completely.
To serve, spoon the fluffy granita into chilled minimalist bowls. Place one or two delicate citrus tuiles alongside. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Arroz con Pollo
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Arroz con Pollo presented on a clean white porcelain plate. Two whole, bone-in chicken thighs with deeply browned, crispy skin sit atop a bed of golden, saffron-stained rice. The rice grains are plump and distinct, interspersed with fine bits of softened onion and concentrated red tomato. The dish shows vibrant yellow and orange hues from the saffron and paprika. A generous sprinkle of bright green, finely chopped parsley is scattered over the top. A single lemon wedge is placed neatly on the side. The plate sits on a light oak wooden table with a folded white cotton napkin. Lighting is bright, natural, and even, highlighting the textures of the crispy skin and the moist rice grains.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of Alioli (garlic mayonnaise)
Accompany with crusty bread and a glass of chilled white wine
Present in a traditional terracotta cazuela for family-style dining
instructions: Season chicken thighs with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a wide shallow pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken skin-side down until golden and crispy.
Flip and brown the other side. Remove chicken from pan.
Add onion to the same pan. Sauté until translucent.
Stir in garlic and grated tomato. Cook until liquid evaporates and mixture darkens.
Add smoked paprika and rice. Stir to coat rice in oil for 2 minutes.
Pour in white wine. Deglaze the pan. Simmer until wine reduces by half.
Add hot stock and saffron. Stir once to distribute.
Place chicken thighs back into the pan on top of the rice.
Simmer undisturbed over medium-low heat for 18-20 minutes.
Ensure chicken reaches internal temperature of 75°C.
Remove from heat. Cover with a clean cloth. Rest for 5 minutes.
Garnish with fresh parsley before serving.
notes: Do not stir the rice once the stock is added to allow a crust to form on the bottom.
Use a wide pan to ensure even rice cooking.

recipes.recipe_name: Seared Cod with Mole-Inspired Chocolate-Chipotle Sauce
recipes.visual_description: A single pan-seared cod fillet, golden-brown and whole, rests centrally on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The fish displays a crisp, flaky texture. A rich, glossy, deep brown mole-inspired chocolate-chipotle sauce is artfully spooned beside the cod, forming a smooth, inviting pool. Fresh, vibrant green cilantro leaves are scattered sparingly over the sauce, providing a bright color contrast. A small, bright lime wedge is placed beside the fish. The presentation is professional and approachable, with moderate negative space. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a simple wooden table surface, a white cotton napkin, and natural, even lighting. The background is minimal, highlighting the dish as the sole focus. The cod is presented as a whole piece, unsliced.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas for scooping the sauce.
Accompany with a side of Mexican red rice or simple black beans.

ingredients.name: Cod fillets, skin on or off
Chipotle peppers in adobo sauce, minced (adjust to taste)

instructions: Pat cod fillets dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and black pepper.

Heat 15ml olive oil in a large non-stick pan over medium heat. Sear cod fillets, skin-side down if applicable, for 4-5 minutes until golden brown and crisp. Flip and cook for another 3-4 minutes until cooked through. Remove fish from pan and set aside.

In the same pan, add remaining 15ml olive oil. Add diced yellow onion and sauté for 5 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic, minced chipotle peppers, tomato paste, ground cumin, dried oregano, and ground cinnamon. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Pour in chicken broth, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan. Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low.

Stir in chopped dark chocolate and unsalted butter until fully melted and the sauce is smooth and glossy. If the sauce is too thick, add a splash more broth. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and lime juice.

To serve, spoon a generous amount of the mole-inspired sauce onto the center of each plate. Carefully place a seared cod fillet on top or beside the sauce. Garnish with fresh chopped cilantro and a lime wedge.
notes: The richness of the dark chocolate provides depth and balances the smokiness of the chipotle, not making the sauce sweet.
This sauce is versatile and can also be used with chicken or pork.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Sun-dried Tomato and Broccoli Pasta
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant single serving of creamy pasta, expertly plated in a clean white porcelain bowl. Al dente rigatoni is coated in a rich, velvety sun-dried tomato cream sauce, its deep orange-red hue contrasting beautifully with bright green, tender-crisp roasted broccoli florets. Finely diced onion and minced garlic are subtly integrated into the sauce. The dish is garnished with fresh, vibrant green basil leaves and a generous dusting of finely grated Parmesan cheese. The pasta is naturally tangled, allowing some negative space. The bowl rests on a simple light wooden table, accompanied by a silver fork and a folded white cotton napkin. Lighting is natural and even, highlighting the dish's fresh textures and inviting colors against a subtly blurred bistro-style background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread for dipping into the sauce.
Accompany with a simple green salad dressed with vinaigrette.
Pair with a light-bodied Italian white wine, such as Pinot Grigio.
instructions: Boil pasta in salted water until al dente. Reserve 250ml pasta water. Drain pasta.
Cut broccoli into small florets. Toss with 15ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Roast on a baking sheet at 200°C for 12-15 minutes until tender-crisp.
Dice onion. Mince garlic. Roughly chop sun-dried tomatoes.

Heat remaining 15ml olive oil in a large pan over medium heat. Sauté diced onion until translucent, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic and chopped sun-dried tomatoes. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Pour in chicken broth and heavy cream. Bring to a gentle simmer. Reduce heat to low.
Stir in 80g grated Parmesan cheese until melted and the sauce is smooth. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Add cooked pasta and roasted broccoli to the sauce in the pan. Toss gently to combine all ingredients.
If the sauce is too thick, add reserved pasta water, 50ml at a time, until the desired creamy consistency is achieved.
Serve immediately in individual bowls. Garnish with fresh basil leaves and additional grated Parmesan cheese.
notes: Ensure pasta is cooked al dente for best texture.
Adjust sauce consistency using reserved pasta water as needed.
Taste and adjust seasoning before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Vanilla Bean Panna Cotta, Strawberry Vodka Gel, Basil Tuile
recipes.visual_description: A single, pristine vanilla bean panna cotta, perfectly unmolded, stands as a creamy white dome at the center of a large, round bone china plate. Its surface is smooth and subtly glossy. Around the base of the panna cotta, two to three translucent, ruby-red shards of strawberry vodka gel are artfully placed, catching the light with their vibrant hue. A delicate, irregular basil tuile, its color a deep, verdant green, is perched elegantly beside the panna cotta, offering a visual and textural counterpoint. The composition is minimalist and architectural, with abundant white space on the plate emphasizing each element's precision. The plate rests on a smooth, cool grey marble surface, reflecting subtle light. A pristine white linen napkin, precisely folded into a triangle, is positioned to the side. Dramatic, focused lighting creates soft shadows, highlighting the dish's contours and luxurious simplicity.
instructions: For the Vanilla Bean Panna Cotta: Bloom gelatin sheets in cold water for 5 minutes.
Split vanilla bean lengthwise. Scrape seeds into a saucepan with heavy cream and 100g sugar. Add vanilla pod.
Heat cream mixture over medium heat until simmering. Do not boil.
Remove from heat. Discard vanilla pod. Squeeze excess water from gelatin. Stir gelatin into hot cream until dissolved.
Pour panna cotta mixture into 4 desired serving molds (e.g., small dome molds or ramekins). Chill for at least 4 hours, or until set.
For the Strawberry Vodka Gel: Wash and hull strawberries. Puree strawberries until smooth. Pass through a fine-mesh sieve to remove seeds.
Combine strawberry puree, strawberry vodka, 30g sugar, and agar-agar powder in a small saucepan.
Bring to a boil, stirring constantly. Simmer for 2 minutes. Pour mixture onto a shallow tray or plate to a thickness of 3-4 mm.
Chill until firmly set, about 30 minutes. Once set, cut the gel into desired shapes (e.g., small squares or irregular shards).
For the Basil Tuile: Preheat oven to 160°C (325°F). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Blanch basil leaves in boiling water for 10 seconds. Immediately transfer to an ice bath. Drain well and pat very dry.
Blend blanched basil leaves, icing sugar, egg white, and melted butter until completely smooth. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve.
Spread a very thin layer of basil batter onto the prepared baking sheet using an offset spatula. Create delicate, irregular shapes.
Bake for 5-7 minutes, or until edges are crisp and golden. Watch carefully as they burn quickly. Remove from oven. Let cool completely on the sheet. They will crisp as they cool.
To Serve: Carefully unmold each panna cotta onto the center of a chilled plate.
Artistically arrange 3-4 pieces of strawberry vodka gel around the panna cotta, leaving ample negative space.
Delicately place one or two basil tuiles on or next to the panna cotta for height and texture contrast.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Tomato and Mozzarella Chicken Pasta
recipes.visual_description: A single generous serving of Creamy Tomato and Mozzarella Chicken Pasta is presented on a round, clean white porcelain dinner plate. Penne pasta, cooked al dente, is gently mounded and tossed with a vibrant, creamy tomato sauce. Succulent 3 cm pan-seared chicken breast chunks are nestled within and around the pasta, their golden-brown crust contrasting with the rich sauce. Melted, glistening mozzarella cheese strands are interwoven throughout the dish. Diced onion and minced garlic are subtly visible within the sauce. The dish is garnished with fresh, vibrant green basil leaves, providing a pop of color. The plate rests on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by standard silver flatware and a folded white cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and colors.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of crusty Italian bread for dipping in the sauce.
Pair with a simple green salad dressed with vinaigrette.
instructions: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Cook penne pasta according to package directions until al dente. Drain, reserve 120 ml pasta water. Set aside.
Cut chicken breasts into 3 cm chunks. Season chicken generously with salt and black pepper.

Heat olive oil in a large skillet or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add chicken chunks. Sear chicken for 4-5 minutes until golden brown on all sides and cooked through. Internal temperature must reach 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion to the skillet. Sauté for 3-4 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in canned diced tomatoes and heavy cream. Bring to a gentle simmer. Cook for 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until sauce slightly thickens.
Return cooked chicken to the skillet with the sauce. Add cooked pasta. Toss to combine. If sauce is too thick, add reserved pasta water, 30 ml at a time, until desired consistency.
Tear fresh mozzarella into small pieces. Stir mozzarella into the pasta mixture until melted and creamy. Taste and adjust seasoning.
Serve immediately. Garnish with fresh basil leaves and grated Parmesan cheese.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
The reserved pasta water helps emulsify the sauce and adjust its consistency.

recipes.recipe_name: Mediterranean Herb-Roasted Chicken with Crispy Potatoes and Asparagus
recipes.visual_description: A single individual portion of Mediterranean Herb-Roasted Chicken is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. A golden-brown, crispy-skinned roasted chicken thigh is the centerpiece, positioned slightly off-center. Around the chicken, a rustic yet organized arrangement of crispy golden potato wedges, vibrant green asparagus spears, and glistening red blistered cherry tomatoes is artfully placed. Thick wedges of roasted red onion are interspersed, adding depth. All ingredients retain their distinct shapes from being roasted: whole chicken thigh, potato wedges, whole asparagus spears, whole tomatoes, and thick onion wedges. A light drizzle of pan juices or olive oil coats the elements. The dish is garnished simply with a few fresh sprigs of rosemary and thyme, and a bright yellow lemon wedge rests beside the chicken. The plate sits on a simple wooden table surface, with a folded cotton napkin and standard flatware positioned beside it. Natural, even lighting highlights the textures and colors, creating an inviting, professional yet approachable casual dining scene.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (390°F). Line a large baking tray with parchment paper.

Wash and halve or quarter baby potatoes into uniform wedges. In a large bowl, toss potatoes with 30ml olive oil, half the smashed garlic, chopped rosemary, salt, and pepper. Spread potatoes in a single layer on the prepared baking tray.
Roast potatoes for 20 minutes.
While potatoes roast, pat chicken thighs dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and pepper.
After 20 minutes, remove tray from oven. Push potatoes to one side. Place chicken thighs, skin-side up, on the empty side of the tray. Return to oven and roast for another 20 minutes.
Trim woody ends from asparagus spears. In the same bowl, toss asparagus, cherry tomatoes, red onion wedges, remaining smashed garlic, 30ml olive oil, chopped thyme, salt, and pepper.
Remove tray from oven again. Arrange seasoned asparagus, tomatoes, and onion around the chicken and potatoes. Ensure chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F).
Return tray to oven and roast for a final 15-20 minutes, or until chicken skin is crispy, vegetables are tender-crisp, and potatoes are golden.
Remove tray from oven. Let chicken rest on the tray for 5 minutes before serving.
Serve immediately with fresh lemon wedges.

recipes.recipe_name: Korean Gochujang Glazed Chicken
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Korean Gochujang Glazed Chicken is presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate. Thick chunks of boneless chicken thigh, deeply caramelized with a glossy, vibrant red-orange gochujang glaze, are artfully arranged. The chicken exhibits subtle charring from searing. Bright green roasted broccoli florets and vivid red bell pepper strips add contrasting color and texture, tender-crisp. The dish is garnished with toasted white sesame seeds and finely sliced green onion. The composition is balanced with appropriate negative space. The plate rests on a simple light wooden table. A ceramic rice bowl with fluffy white rice sits beside it, accompanied by elegant chopsticks and a folded cotton napkin. Natural, even light illuminates the scene, with a soft, blurred restaurant background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of steamed white rice
Accompany with various banchan (small side dishes) like kimchi or pickled radish

ingredients.name: Red bell pepper, cut into strips

instructions: Cook white rice according to package directions. Keep warm.
Cut chicken thighs into 3-4 cm thick chunks. Pat dry with paper towels.
In a medium bowl, combine gochujang, soy sauce, honey, rice vinegar, sesame oil, minced garlic, and grated ginger. Whisk well to create the glaze.
Add chicken chunks to 2/3 of the glaze. Toss to coat thoroughly. Marinate chicken for at least 30 minutes at room temperature, or up to 2 hours in the refrigerator.
Preheat oven to 200°C (390°F).
Toss broccoli florets and red bell pepper strips with 15 ml vegetable oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking sheet.
Roast vegetables for 15-20 minutes, or until tender-crisp and slightly charred.
Heat 15 ml vegetable oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear marinated chicken chunks in a single layer for 3-4 minutes per side, until browned. Do not overcrowd the pan; cook in batches if necessary.
Transfer skillet to the preheated oven. Bake for 10-12 minutes, or until internal temperature of chicken reaches 75°C (167°F).
Remove chicken from oven. Add remaining 1/3 of the glaze to the skillet. Toss chicken to coat evenly in the hot glaze.
Serve chicken and roasted vegetables immediately with warm white rice.
Garnish with toasted sesame seeds and thinly sliced green onions.
notes: Adjust the amount of gochujang to control the spice level.
For extra richness, use bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs and adjust cooking time.

recipes.recipe_name: Mediterranean Roasted Chicken with Lemon and Herbs
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Mediterranean Roasted Chicken is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. Two golden-brown, crispy-skinned chicken thighs are the centerpiece, nestled among vibrant roasted vegetables. Small new potatoes, halved and roasted to a tender, slightly crisp exterior, are scattered around. Burst cherry tomatoes add pops of bright red. Red onion wedges, caramelized at the edges, and whole smashed garlic cloves are interspersed. Fresh rosemary and thyme sprigs are casually placed, contributing deep green color and aromatic appeal. Thin lemon slices, slightly charred, rest atop the chicken. The dish exhibits natural textures and rich, warm colors. The plate sits on a simple light wooden table surface, accompanied by a folded cotton napkin and standard flatware, under soft, natural lighting, evoking a modern bistro setting.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Line a large baking tray with parchment paper.
Pat chicken thighs dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Halve small new potatoes. Quarter red onion into wedges. Smash garlic cloves.
Slice one lemon into thin rounds. Juice the second lemon.
On the baking tray, combine chicken, potatoes, red onion, garlic, cherry tomatoes, and Kalamata olives.
Drizzle with olive oil. Add fresh rosemary and thyme sprigs. Toss to coat evenly.
Arrange ingredients in a single layer. Distribute lemon slices over the chicken and vegetables.
Roast for 45-55 minutes, or until chicken skin is golden and crispy, and internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F).
Stir vegetables halfway through roasting for even browning.
Remove from oven. Drizzle with fresh lemon juice. Let rest for 5 minutes before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Seared King Oyster Mushroom, Smoked Potato Puree, Caramelized Onion, Parmesan Crisp
